target.title: fix(cron): failure alerts to a channel are dropped when a global webhook failure destination is set
target.body:
Closes #102235

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a cron job with a channel-shaped failure destination and no explicit mode (e.g. `--failure-channel slack --failure-to "#alerts"` with no `--failure-mode`) would silently inherit a global `cron.failureDestination` webhook mode. At failure time the chat target was fed to the webhook URL validator, failed, and the failure alert was dropped with only a "webhook URL is invalid, skipping" log — the operator never learns the job's failures are unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveFailureDestination` only reconciled the mode when the job's `mode` field was present, so a mode-less channel override kept the inherited global `webhook` mode. The fix treats a channel-shaped override without a mode as an announce destination — matching primary-delivery semantics, where `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` defaults a missing mode to `announce` — and reuses the existing cross-mode rule so an inherited global webhook URL is not carried into the announce plan. A to-only override (no channel, no mode) intentionally still inherits the global mode, since a bare `to` with a global webhook default is a webhook URL override.

## User Impact

Cron failure alerts routed with `--failure-channel <channel> --failure-to <target>` (and no `--failure-mode`) now reach the named channel even when a global webhook failure destination is configured. Explicit-mode overrides and to-only URL overrides behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Three regression tests added in `src/cron/delivery.test.ts`:
- the issue's repro: global `{ mode: "webhook", to: "https://hook..." }` + job `{ channel: "slack", to: "#alerts" }` resolves to `{ mode: "announce", channel: "slack", to: "#alerts" }` (previously `{ mode: "webhook", to: "#alerts" }`, dropped downstream)
- a channel-only override clears the inherited webhook URL instead of announcing to it
- a to-only override still inherits the global webhook mode with the overridden URL

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now work through Signal-owned reply-author resolution instead of adding a shared `replyToAuthor` field to every outbound channel path. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies record the inbound Signal sender by conversation and message timestamp so later Signal sends can attach the native quote metadata.

The only core behavior change is scoped to Signal send actions: when the Signal message action receives an explicit `replyToId`, it is treated as the reply target and wins over an inline `[[reply_to:...]]` directive.

## What Changed

- Signal outbound sends: message adapter, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal inbound messages: accepted inbound messages register `{account, conversation, message timestamp} -> sender author` for Signal group native reply lookup.
- Signal reply-author lookup: new Signal helper keeps a bounded in-process author cache and uses the existing optional Signal runtime store hook when available.
- Signal message action: `replyToId` is accepted as a Signal-only alias for explicit reply targets during message-action normalization.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` derive native quote authors as `+15551234567` and `username:alice`.
- Group Signal replies resolve the quote author from the Signal-owned author cache instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Signal inbound context tests prove a group message stores the sender author under its Signal message timestamp.
- Signal message-action normalization tests prove `replyToId` is only treated as a reply target alias for the Signal channel, and explicit `replyTo` still wins when both fields are present.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

target.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy
target.body:
Closes #102206

> **AI-assisted PR.** Authored with Claude (Opus 4.8). I have reviewed the change and understand what it does.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent running on the embedded Codex backend would have its autonomous notifications to other channels **silently denied**. Since v2026.6.9, heartbeat and cron polls, plus `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs, cannot send a message to a different provider (e.g. a heartbeat notification to Discord) — the send is dropped by the cross-context messaging guard with no user-visible error. In the reporting environment this silently lost **71 real notifications over ~2.5 weeks**.

The affected surface is autonomous/background delivery from a Codex-backed agent (heartbeat, cron, inter-session handoff) to any channel other than the one the agent's main session is nominally on. Interactive WebChat UI conversations are not the trigger and their behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Mechanism.** Since v2026.6.9 the Codex app-server dynamic-tool bridge passes `currentChannelProvider: resolveCodexMessageToolProvider(params)` into the hook context. The resolver returned `messageChannel ?? messageProvider`. For internal turns delivered into an agent's main session — heartbeat/cron polls and `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs — the embedded backend passes both fields as the internal `webchat` channel (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`); see `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`. `enforceCrossContextPolicy` then treats the run as *bound to a real `webchat` conversation* and denies an autonomous cross-provider send:

```
Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
```

v2026.6.8 passed **no** binding on the Codex path, so the guard no-op'd (`if (!currentTarget) return`). v2026.6.9 introduced the binding and thus the regression (bisected 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED in the same session).

**Fix.** `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` now returns `undefined` when **both** hold: (a) the resolved provider is the internal message channel (`isInternalMessageChannel`), and (b) the turn is an internal turn — `trigger === "heartbeat" | "cron"`, or `inputProvenance.kind === "inter_session"` (new exported helper `isInternalCodexMessageTurn`). This restores the pre-v2026.6.9 "no binding" behavior for exactly the turns that regressed.

**Why the turn-kind discriminator is the narrowest correct scope.** Dropping the binding *only* for internal turns on the internal channel leaves every real conversation bound:
- Real WebChat UI conversations carry a `user`/`manual` trigger and no inter-session provenance, so they **stay bound** — cross-provider containment for the genuine user-facing surface is unchanged.
- Internal turns delivered on a real deliverable channel (e.g. `telegram`) are not on the internal `webchat` channel, so they also **stay bound**.
- Only the spurious binding to the non-deliverable internal channel — which never represented a real conversation to contain against — is removed. `toolPolicyMessageProvider` still carries the raw channel, so channel-level tool policy resolution is unaffected.

This aligns the Codex path with the non-Codex core path, which never binds internal turns to the internal channel in the first place. The same resolver feeds both `run-attempt.ts` and `side-question.ts`, so both Codex code paths are covered by the single change.

## User Impact

Operators running agents on the embedded Codex backend get their autonomous notifications delivered again: heartbeat and cron runs, and inter-session (`sessions_send`) handoffs, can once more send to channels other than the agent's nominal channel (Discord, Telegram, etc.) instead of being silently suppressed. No configuration change is required, and no new denial or prompt-injection surface is opened — interactive WebChat UI conversations keep the exact same cross-provider containment they have today.

## Relationship to #102216 / #102217

Two PRs are already open on #102206. Both are worthwhile attempts at the same regression; this one differs in what it fixes and what it preserves.

- **#102216** (@lin-hongkuan) returns `messageProvider` when `messageChannel === "webchat" && messageProvider !== "webchat"`. This does not fix the reported bug: embedded-backend internal runs pass **both** fields as `INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` (`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`), so `messageProvider` is also `"webchat"` and the guard condition never triggers for a real heartbeat/cron/inter-session turn — the resolver still returns `"webchat"` and the send is still denied. Its added test uses `{ messageChannel: "webchat", messageProvider: "discord" }`, a combination internal runs do not produce.
- **#102217** (@xydigit-zt, [AI]) strips `"webchat"` from the resolver **unconditionally**. That does fix the denial, but it also removes the binding for genuine WebChat UI user conversations, loosening cross-provider containment for a real user-facing surface (the PR carries `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`). This PR scopes the drop to internal turns only (`isInternalCodexMessageTurn`), so real WebChat UI turns keep their binding and containment is unchanged.

In short: this change fixes the exact turns that regressed (which #102216 misses) without loosening the guard for real user conversations (which #102217 does).

## Evidence

**1. Production occurrence.** See the live logs in #102206: 71 lost notifications over ~2.5 weeks, the exact denial string above, and the bisection showing the same session going 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED.

**2. Real-runtime differential** (compiled `dist`, default-deny config, no `crossContext` overrides). `enforceCrossContextPolicy` is byte-identical across the two builds — only the resolver changed. A harness drove the real pipeline `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider → enforceCrossContextPolicy({ action: "send", channel: "discord", ... })`:

| Turn | BEFORE (installed OpenClaw 2026.6.11, `e085fa1`) | AFTER (this branch, `b279803`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heartbeat → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".` | resolver → `undefined`; gate no-ops; **send passes** |
| Inter-session (`sessions_send`) → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** (same denial) | resolver → `undefined`; **send passes** |
| **Control:** genuine WebChat *user* turn → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** (containment for the real UI surface unchanged) |

(Real Discord channel ids redacted as `channel:<redacted>`.)

Note: full-gateway E2E was not run because the embedded Codex credential is keychain-backed OAuth and is not isolatable without touching the production keychain. The changed logic is fully exercised at the provider layer, where the regression lives.

**3. Tests.** 6 new regression tests:

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`
- `keeps the internal channel bound for real webchat user turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for heartbeat and cron turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for sessions_send inter-session turns`
- `keeps a real delivery channel bound even for internal triggers`
- `classifies internal-turn kinds for cross-context binding`

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
- `does not bind the message tool to the internal channel for internal turns`

Focused vitest green: `dynamic-tool-build` 56/56, `run-attempt` 118/118, `outbound-policy` 25/25. `pnpm build` green.

Template variables are not populated when user issues early stop commands. 

- **Problem:** When a user sends a "stop" command (e.g. on WhatsApp), the abort reply displays unresolved template variables: `{model} - {thinkingLevel} 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`
- **Why it matters:** The raw `{model}` and `{thinkingLevel}` placeholders leak into user-facing messages, looking broken and confusing.
- **What changed:** `createReplyPrefixContext()` now pre-seeds the `ResponsePrefixContext` with model, provider, and thinkingLevel resolved from config defaults, so early-exit paths like abort have valid values for template interpolation.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** No changes to abort logic, dispatch flow, template resolution engine, or `formatAbortReplyText()`. The `onModelSelected()` callback still overwrites the defaults at runtime during normal replies.

target.title: security: gateway public network hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive security hardening for OpenClaw Gateway when exposed to public networks (e.g. `https://openclaw.allegro.earth/`). The existing security mechanisms (non-loopback auth enforcement, auth rate limiting, CORS checks) leave gaps that this PR addresses:

- **IP access control** (allowlist/blocklist with CIDR support) — enforced on both HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades, loopback always allowed, blocklist takes priority
- **Password/token strength validation** — CRITICAL startup warnings when network-exposed with short tokens (<32 chars) or weak passwords (<12 chars, all-digit/all-letter patterns)
- **TLS enforcement check** — CRITICAL startup warning when network-exposed without TLS and no `terminatedUpstream` declaration
- **Per-IP request rate limiting** — sliding window (default 120 req/min/IP), loopback exempt by default, returns 429 with Retry-After
- **Auth audit logging** — JSONL to `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-auth.jsonl` with file rotation, records `auth_failure`, `auth_success`, `rate_limited`, `ip_blocked` events
- **Auto HSTS** — `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` set automatically when TLS is enabled
- **Eliminate silent 0.0.0.0 fallback** — `loopback`, `tailnet`, and `custom` bind modes now throw clear errors instead of silently falling back to all-interfaces
- **New security audit checks** — `gateway.no_tls_network_exposed` (critical), `gateway.password_too_short` (critical), `gateway.password_weak_pattern` (warn), `gateway.no_request_rate_limit` (warn), `gateway.auto_bind_fallback` (warn)
- **Enhanced `doctor` warnings** — TLS, password strength, token length, request rate limit checks for network-exposed gateways

### Config additions (`gateway.*`)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `ipAllowlist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP allowlist (loopback always allowed) |
| `ipBlocklist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP blocklist (checked before allowlist) |
| `requestRateLimit.maxRequests` | `number` | 120 | Max requests per IP per window |
| `requestRateLimit.windowMs` | `number` | 60000 | Sliding window duration (ms) |
| `requestRateLimit.exemptLoopback` | `boolean` | true | Skip rate limiting for localhost |
| `tls.terminatedUpstream` | `boolean` | false | Declare TLS terminated by reverse proxy |

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — type check passes
- [x] New unit tests: `ip-access-control.test.ts` (9 tests), `request-rate-limit.test.ts` (7 tests), `auth-audit-log.test.ts` (4 tests), `credential-strength.test.ts` (9 tests)
- [x] Existing tests updated and passing: `server-runtime-config.test.ts`, `doctor-security.test.ts`, `net.test.ts`, `auth.test.ts`, `audit.test.ts` — 245 tests total
- [ ] Manual: start gateway with `bind=lan` and verify startup warnings
- [ ] Manual: test IP blocklist returns 403
- [ ] Manual: test request rate limit returns 429

target.title: feat(github-copilot): support GitHub Enterprise data-residency Copilot auth
target.body:
> **AI-assisted PR.** Implemented with the GitHub Copilot CLI (Claude). The author has reviewed and understands all changes; validated locally (targeted Vitest suites, `tsgo` typecheck, oxlint/oxfmt, SDK surface budget) and against a live `*.ghe.com` tenant (see Evidence). ## What Problem This Solves Organizations on a data-residency GitHub Enterprise tenant (a `*.ghe.com` host such as `your-org.ghe.com`) could not use GitHub Copilot with OpenClaw. Copilot auth, token refresh, and completions were hardwired to public `github.com` / `api.github.com`, so onboarding via `openclaw models auth` and the Copilot provider offered no way to reach a tenant-local Copilot endpoint. Enterprise users were effectively locked out of the Copilot provider. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds GitHub Enterprise (data residency) as a first-class Copilot auth choice, nested alongside the existing GitHub and Local Proxy options. Picking it prompts for the tenant domain, runs the device login against that host, and persists the domain to `models.providers.github-copilot.params.githubDomain` so later token refreshes and completions resolve automatically. Domain resolution follows `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` env > config > `github.com`. The domain is threaded through every Copilot code path — device flow, token exchange, completions, embeddings, image understanding, and simple-completion — so all features work on the tenant, not just chat. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged (no config is written for the default host). No config schema change (uses free-form provider params). **Security (fail-closed by design):** the host allowlist is locked to `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` tenants only — any other value (typo or injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN`/config) falls back to `github.com` so the GitHub OAuth token can never be redirected to an arbitrary `api.`. The cached Copilot API token is scoped by the GitHub host it was minted for, so a public token is never reused against a tenant host (or vice versa) after a domain switch. **Domain-switch re-authentication:** onboarding no longer reuses a stored Copilot token when the selected domain differs from the one the token was minted under. Any switch (public `github.com` ↔ a `*.ghe.com` tenant, or one tenant to another) forces a fresh device login so the persisted `githubDomain` always matches a tenant-scoped token; re-running login for the *same* domain still offers to reuse the current token. Switching back to public `github.com` clears the persisted `githubDomain` so config returns to the default (no config == `github.com`). This closes the gap where declining re-login could write a tenant domain against an unverified public token. ## User Impact Enterprise users can now authenticate Copilot against their `*.ghe.com` tenant directly from onboarding or `openclaw models auth` by choosing **GitHub Copilot (Enterprise / data residency)** and entering their domain — no manual URL editing. Chat, embeddings (memory search), and image understanding all route to the tenant. `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` enables fully headless/CI setups. Non-enterprise users see no change. ## Scope & Related Work Closes #102219. This PR extends the **existing bundled `github-copilot` provider** with data-residency domain support for the auth, token-exchange, and completions paths it already ships. It does **not** add a new provider, a new model catalog, or a config-schema change (it uses free-form provider params). Related: #96988 ("GHE.com Model Integration"), which was closed NOT_PLANNED and routed to ClawHub/plugin scope. That issue asked for a broader/new GHE model integration; this change is deliberately narrower: it makes the provider OpenClaw already bundles honor an allowlisted, fail-closed `*.ghe.com` tenant host so enterprise users are not locked out, without introducing new SDK provider surface. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged. **AI-assisted:** developed and validated with AI coding agents (Copilot, Claude) under human direction; all changes human-reviewed, with live tenant validation run by the author. ## Evidence Live validation against a real data-residency GHE tenant (domain/token redacted): ### [P1] GHE Login, Token Refresh & Completion — Redacted Evidence 1. GHE Login / Auth pre-warm (gateway startup, 18:56:23 UTC) ``` subsystem=gateway level=INFO time=2026-07-02T18:56:23.756Z provider auth state pre-warmed in 477ms eventLoopMax=11.9ms ``` Stored GHE credential loaded and validated successfully on gateway boot. 2. Active GHE Copilot token state ``` integrationId: vscode-chat token: [REDACTED] updatedAt: 2026-07-02T21:03:31Z ← refreshed ~12 minutes ago expiresAt: 2026-07-02T21:33:31Z ← valid for ~17 more minutes expired? false ``` Standard 30-minute Copilot token TTL confirmed; token was refreshed mid-session against REDACTED.ghe.com. 3. Completion calls against GHE endpoint (sample) ``` subsystem=provider-transport-fetch level=INFO time=2026-07-02T21:09:19Z [model-fetch] start provider=github-copilot api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-4.6 method=POST url=https://copilot-api.REDACTED.ghe.com/v1/messages status=— [model-fetch] response provider=github-copilot api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-4.6 status=200 elapsedMs=1529 contentType=text/event-stream ``` Dozens of successful round-trips throughout the session (18:56 → 21:15 UTC), all status=200.

Re-run login? ``` **S4 — Domain switch forces re-authentication both ways, and clears/restores config** Tenant → public (no reuse offered, fresh device login forced): ``` │ Switching back to github.com requires a new login to authorize Copilot for the public │ domain. ``` After the public login, the persisted `githubDomain` was removed from config (verified via the config backup snapshot). Public → tenant then forced a fresh tenant login and re-persisted the domain: ``` │ Switching to redactedorg.ghe.com requires a new tenant login to authorize Copilot for that │ domain. ``` **S5 — Embeddings (memory search) via the tenant** With `memorySearch.provider: "github-copilot"`, `openclaw memory index --force` embedded the seeded memory files through the tenant: ``` Memory Search (main) Provider: github-copilot (requested: github-copilot) Indexed: 2/2 files · 2 chunks Index identity: index was built for model text-embedding-3-small Embedding cache: enabled (2 entries) Batch: disabled (failures 0/2) ``` The embedding model (`text-embedding-3-small`) was auto-discovered live from the tenant Copilot catalog, and the domain-stamped token cache introduced by this PR shows the Copilot API token used was minted via the tenant exchange: ```json { "domain": "redactedorg.ghe.com", "integrationId": "vscode-chat" } ``` **Automated checks (all green on the current head, locally before push; CI re-runs them):** - `pnpm test extensions/github-copilot` (full extension lane incl. contract seams), `pnpm test:contracts:plugins`, touched core tests (`provider-auth`, `registry.contract`, `simple-completion-runtime`, `image`). - tsgo (core + extensions), oxlint, oxfmt, plugin-SDK surface-budget guard, import-boundary inventories, import-cycle check, full `pnpm build`. - Docs added: "GitHub Enterprise (data residency)" section in `docs/providers/github-copilot.md`. **Addressed in review:** - Locked the domain allowlist to `github.com` + `*.ghe.com` (fail closed) and scoped the Copilot token cache by domain, per ClawSweeper's two P1 findings. - Shortcut login (`login-github-copilot`) now persists the domain it minted the token for (and clears a stale tenant domain on public logins), so a tenant token can never be left routing to github.com after `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` is unset; docs updated to match. target.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `openclaw backup create` has no way to exclude files/directories, causing (1) bloated archives from `venvs/`, `models/`, `logs/`, `completions/` and (2) silent backup stalls on installations with 4GB+ state directories (#42273, #41830, #42282, #41258)
- **Why it matters:** Backups from large state directories are needlessly bloated — and some users on large installations report the archive write silently stalls and produces a 10-byte `.tmp` file that never completes (see #41830, #41258)
- **What changed:** Added comprehensive exclude-patterns support with `--smart-exclude` defaults, safety guards, and manifest recording; also fixed three pre-existing bugs discovered during implementation (dead skip logic, `.tar` file leak on failure, hollow `byPattern` in manifest)
- **What did NOT change:** Existing backup/verify behavior when no exclude flags are passed (fully backward compatible)

> **Note on GitHub Discussion:** CONTRIBUTING.md recommends opening a Discussion for new features before a PR. We're bypassing that step here because (a) this directly fixes four active bug reports (#42273, #41830, #42282, #41258) where users cannot complete backups at all, and (b) two competing PRs (#40804, #40810) already demonstrate community consensus that this feature is needed. A Discussion would duplicate that existing context.

## Change Type

- [x] Feature
- [x] Bug Fix

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] CLI

## Linked Issues/PRs

- Closes #40786 — Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI
- Fixes #42273 — backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)
- Fixes #41830 — Bug: `openclaw backup create` stalls — produces 10-byte .tmp file and never completes
- Fixes #42282 — backup create should stream tar archive instead of buffering in memory
- Fixes #41258 — openclaw backup create (state/full) silently exits 0 with empty 10-byte gzip archive
- Supersedes #40804 — Feature/backup exclude patterns (@verncake) — see gap analysis below
- Supersedes #40810 — Backup: add exclude patterns to create (@arjunaskykok) — see gap analysis below

## New CLI Flags

| Flag                        | Description                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--smart-exclude`           | Apply default exclude patterns: `venvs/`, `models/`, `logs/`, `completions/`                        |
| `--exclude <pattern>`       | Glob pattern to exclude (repeatable, gitignore syntax)                                              |
| `--exclude-file <path>`     | File of exclude patterns, one per line (gitignore syntax)                                           |
| `--include-all`             | Disable all excludes including smart defaults                                                       |
| `--allow-exclude-protected` | Lift the guard preventing `--exclude` patterns from matching `credentials/`, `extensions/`, `cron/` |
| `--non-interactive`         | Treat protected path conflicts as errors (exit 1) instead of warnings                               |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

### Basic usage

```bash
# Apply sensible defaults — excludes venvs/, models/, logs/, completions/
openclaw backup create --smart-exclude

# Custom patterns
openclaw backup create --exclude "*.log" --exclude "**/__pycache__"

# Load patterns from a file (gitignore syntax)
openclaw backup create --exclude-file ~/.openclaw/.backupignore

# Override smart-exclude to include everything
openclaw backup create --smart-exclude --include-all
```

### Auto-detected `.backupignore`

If `~/.openclaw/.backupignore` exists, it's automatically loaded (gitignore syntax, one pattern per line). Security: group/world-writable files are rejected with a warning. Symlinks are rejected.

### Protected path guards

`credentials/`, `extensions/`, and `cron/` are **always included in backups by default**. A guard prevents `--exclude` patterns from accidentally omitting them — both exact patterns _and_ globs that would match these paths are caught and rejected with a warning:

```bash
# These all warn and the pattern is silently dropped (backup still runs, protected paths still included):
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/"
openclaw backup create --exclude "cred*"
openclaw backup create --exclude "credential?"

# Intentionally exclude a protected path — requires explicit opt-out:
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/" --allow-exclude-protected

# Non-interactive mode (for scripts/agents) — exits 1 instead of warning:
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/" --non-interactive
```

### Manifest recording

Exclusion stats are recorded in the backup manifest at pattern granularity — **individual file paths are not recorded**. This avoids leaking sensitive filenames (e.g. `credentials/slack-oauth-token.json`) to remote backup destinations:

```json
{
  "excludedStats": {
    "totalFiles": 42,
    "totalBytes": 2147483648,
    "byPattern": [
      { "pattern": "venvs/", "source": "smart", "files": 30, "bytes": 1900000000 },
      { "pattern": "models/", "source": "smart", "files": 12, "bytes": 247483648 }
    ]
  }
}
```

> **Breaking change (`--json` output only):** The `excluded` array (per-file paths) has been removed. Consumers of `backup create --json` should read `excludedStats` instead. Archives created without exclude flags are unaffected.

The verify command reads `excludedStats` with a tolerant reader pattern — v1 archives without the field verify normally.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? **No**
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? **No**
- New/changed network calls? **No**
- Command/tool execution surface changed? **Yes** — New CLI options added
- Data access scope changed? **No**

### Security considerations

| Concern                                                      | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| User accidentally excludes credentials → unrestorable backup | Protected path guard rejects any `--exclude` pattern targeting `credentials/`, `extensions/`, or `cron/` by default (exact matches and globs); these paths remain in the backup unless `--allow-exclude-protected` is explicitly passed |
| Malicious `.backupignore` injected into state dir            | Group/world-writable files are rejected; symlinks are rejected; file must be a regular file ≤1MB                                                                                                                                        |
| Pathological patterns cause ReDoS or filter hangs            | Pattern length (256 char), count (500), and globstar depth (5) limits enforced                                                                                                                                                          |
| Symlink escape via excluded paths                            | `follow: false` in tar options; `ignore` package operates on path strings, not filesystem                                                                                                                                               |
| Filter error silently includes sensitive data                | Fail-closed: any filter error _excludes_ the entry (asymmetric failure prefers safety)                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--exclude-file` pointing to a symlink                       | `lstatSync` detects and rejects symlinked exclude file paths                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Architecture

### New files

| File                                           | Purpose                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/infra/backup-exclude.ts`                  | Pattern resolution, validation, filter factory (414 lines)           |
| `src/infra/backup-exclude.test.ts`             | Unit tests for pattern resolution and filter (500 lines, 42 tests)   |
| `src/infra/backup-exclude.integration.test.ts` | End-to-end archive tests with exclude patterns (562 lines, 15 tests) |

### Modified files

| File                                      | Change                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/infra/backup-create.ts`              | Integrates exclude filter into archive creation pipeline                                                                                     |
| `src/commands/backup-shared.ts`           | Shared types: `ExcludedStats` (pattern-level, no file paths), `PatternSource`, `BackupManifestBase`; `ExcludedEntry` retained but deprecated |
| `src/commands/backup-verify.ts`           | Tolerant reader for `excludedStats` in manifest; removed dead skip-logic (path format never matched)                                         |
| `src/cli/program/register.backup.ts`      | Register new CLI flags                                                                                                                       |
| `src/cli/program/register.backup.test.ts` | CLI forwarding tests                                                                                                                         |

### Pattern matching approach

Uses the [`ignore`](https://github.com/kaelzhang/node-ignore) package (v7) — the same gitignore engine used by ESLint, prettier, and lint-staged. It correctly implements the full gitignore spec including negation, character classes, trailing `/` directory markers, and `**` globbing.

Three-tier matching in the filter (fast → specific):

1. **Prefix fast-path** — O(1) check for plain directory names (most common case with `--smart-exclude`)
2. **`ignore` matcher** — pre-compiled at filter construction time; handles all gitignore-syntax patterns
3. Fail-closed: any error during matching excludes the entry

Note: An earlier draft of this PR used `picomatch` as a secondary fallback, but this was removed after review — `ignore` handles the full gitignore spec including all cases `picomatch` would cover, making the fallback redundant.

### Two-step archive creation

When exclude patterns are active, the archive is created in two steps:

1. Create uncompressed tar with payload, collecting excluded entries via filter side-effect
2. Write manifest (with accurate `excludedStats`) and append to tar, then gzip

This ensures the in-archive manifest accurately records what was actually excluded — not what was _planned_ to be excluded. The no-exclude path remains a single step and is unchanged.

### Post-tar integrity cross-check

Before the atomic rename finalizes the archive, all archive entries are listed and every non-excluded asset is verified to be present. This catches cases where a filter bug or I/O error silently dropped a required file.

## Dependencies

| Package  | Version | Justification                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ignore` | ^7.0.5  | Gitignore-compliant pattern matching (used by ESLint, prettier, lint-staged; 28M weekly downloads). Note: `minimatch` v10.2.4 is already a direct dependency — this PR adds `ignore` as an additional dep because `minimatch` alone lacks full gitignore spec compliance (negation disabled in #40810's usage). |

## Gap Analysis: Why This Supersedes #40804 and #40810

| Feature                                                  | #40804 (@verncake) | #40810 (@arjunaskykok)                      | This PR                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `--exclude` flag                                         | ✅                 | ✅                                          | ✅                          |
| `--exclude-file`                                         | ✅                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `--smart-exclude` defaults (fixes stall bugs)            | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `--include-all` override                                 | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `--allow-exclude-protected`                              | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `--non-interactive` (agent-friendly)                     | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Protected path guard (exact + glob)                      | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Fail-closed filter (error → exclude)                     | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Symlink protection on exclude-file                       | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Pattern validation (ReDoS prevention)                    | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `excludedStats` in manifest (no per-file path leakage)   | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Verify tolerant reader (handles missing `excludedStats`) | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Post-tar integrity cross-check                           | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Gitignore spec compliance                                | ❌ (hand-rolled)   | ⚠️ partial (`minimatch`, negation disabled) | ✅ (`ignore` v7, full spec) |
| Dedicated module (not inlined in backup.ts)              | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Test coverage                                            | ~139 lines         | ~85 lines                                   | 1,221 lines                 |

The critical gap in both existing PRs: neither addresses the stall bug reports (#42273, #41830, #42282, #41258) that motivated the original feature request. This PR's `--smart-exclude` flag directly solves them.

## Pre-existing Bugs Fixed

Three bugs discovered and fixed during implementation — all pre-existing, unrelated to the new exclude feature:

| Bug                                 | Location                                                    | Root Cause                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dead skip logic in verify           | `backup-verify.ts`, `backup-create.ts` post-tar cross-check | `excludedPaths` set stored relative paths; `asset.sourcePath` is absolute — `Set.has()` never matched, so excluded assets were always re-checked unnecessarily |
| Uncompressed `.tar` leak on failure | `backup-create.ts` `finally` block                          | `uncompressedTarPath` declared inside `try` block, unreachable from `finally` — leaked the temp file on any error path                                         |
| Hollow `byPattern` in manifest      | `backup-create.ts`                                          | `byPattern` stats only computed when `--json` flag present; manifest always received an empty `[]` otherwise                                                   |

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.8.0 (x64)
- Runtime: Node.js 25.6.1

### Steps

```bash
# 1. Create a state dir with large directories
mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/{venvs,models,logs,completions}
dd if=/dev/zero of=~/.openclaw/venvs/large-file bs=1M count=100

# 2. Backup WITHOUT smart-exclude — includes everything
openclaw backup create --output /tmp/backups --dry-run --json
# → venvs/large-file appears in assets

# 3. Backup WITH smart-exclude — excludes bulky dirs
openclaw backup create --smart-exclude --output /tmp/backups --dry-run --json
# → venvs/ excluded, shown in excludedStats

# 4. Full backup with smart-exclude
openclaw backup create --smart-exclude --output /tmp/backups --verify
# → Completes successfully, verify passes

# 5. Custom exclude pattern
openclaw backup create --exclude "*.log" --exclude "**/__pycache__" --output /tmp/backups

# 6. Protected path guard (exact match)
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/" --output /tmp/backups
# → Warning: pattern matches protected path

# 7. Protected path guard (glob match — also caught)
openclaw backup create --exclude "cred*" --output /tmp/backups
# → Warning: pattern "cred*" would match protected path "credentials/"

# 8. Override protected path guard
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/" --allow-exclude-protected --output /tmp/backups
```

## Evidence

- [x] Unit tests passing (500 lines, 42 tests)
- [x] Integration tests passing (562 lines, 15 tests)
- [x] CLI forwarding tests passing (159 lines, 10 tests)
- [x] Verify command handles archives with and without `excludedStats`
- [x] Backward compatible with existing archives (missing `excludedStats` field = normal verify)
- [x] 67 backup-related tests passing; full suite pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR

## Human Verification

- Tested with real 11GB `.openclaw` state directory containing `venvs/` (4.2GB), `models/` (3.1GB), `logs/` (2.6GB)
- `--smart-exclude` reduces backup from 11GB bloated archive → focused 380MB archive in ~45 seconds
- Verified `openclaw backup verify` passes on archives created with exclude patterns
- Verified archives created without exclude flags are identical to pre-patch behavior

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — no behavior change when no exclude flags are passed
- Config/env changes? **No**
- Migration needed? **No**
- Existing archives verify correctly with updated verify command

## Risks and Mitigations

| Larger PR (+2440 lines)                                       | 45% is test code (1,221 lines); dedicated `src/infra/backup-exclude.ts` keeps production logic focused                            |

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw had local backup export/verify, but no low-friction folder-backed snapshot flow for encrypted backups plus workspace mirroring.
- Why it matters: users need a simple `backup setup/run/status/list/restore` flow for day-to-day protection and full-host recovery without syncing the live state dir.
- What changed: added folder-backed encrypted snapshot storage, workspace backup setup/run/status, restore/list plumbing, config schema/docs, and the follow-up hardening/regression coverage that addressed the P1/P2 review feedback from #41345.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not add provider-specific cloud APIs, device-identity export/import, or any live state-dir sync behavior.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #32921
- Related #40090
- Related #7598
- Related #41345

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Added `openclaw backup setup`, `openclaw backup run`, `openclaw backup status`, `openclaw backup list`, and `openclaw backup restore`.
- `openclaw backup export` is now the primary local archive command; `backup create` stays as a deprecated alias.
- `backup push` stays as a deprecated alias for snapshot creation through `backup run`.
- `reset` and `uninstall` now recommend `openclaw backup export`.
- Backup config now supports `backup.target` and `backup.encryption.key` for folder-backed encrypted snapshots.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  - Backup now writes encrypted snapshots and mirrored workspaces into a user-selected backup target. Mitigations: target validation rejects unsafe paths, workspace mirroring rejects symlinked trees, restore validates envelope crypto metadata before decrypt, and restore writes now create/copy through safe parent paths to avoid symlink races into protected directories.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / pnpm workspace
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): `backup.target=<temp dir>`, `backup.encryption.key=<redacted>`

### Steps

1. Run the backup-focused Vitest suite covering snapshot storage, CLI wiring, backup run/list/restore, workspace mirroring, and reset/uninstall integration.
2. Run `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` on the rebased branch.
3. Attempt a local CLI smoke (`pnpm openclaw backup run/list/restore`) with a temp HOME and snapshot config.

### Expected

- Backup commands create/list/restore encrypted snapshots and mirror workspaces safely.
- Build/check pass unless blocked by unrelated main-branch issues.
- Local CLI smoke exercises the new flow end-to-end.

### Actual

- The backup-focused Vitest suite passed.
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm check`, and the local CLI smoke are currently blocked by unrelated `main` breakage after rebasing: `@mariozechner/pi-ai` no longer exports `getOAuthApiKey`, `getOAuthProviders`, or `loginOpenAICodex`, which breaks `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts`, `src/commands/openai-codex-oauth.ts`, and several agent wrapper files before backup code runs.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Commands run:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run src/commands/backup.test.ts src/commands/backup-run.test.ts src/commands/backup-verify.test.ts src/commands/backup-status.test.ts src/commands/backup-snapshot.test.ts src/commands/backup-restore.test.ts src/commands/workspace-backup.test.ts src/backup/snapshot-store/config.test.ts src/backup/snapshot-store/encryption.test.ts src/backup/snapshot-store/provider-folder.test.ts src/backup/snapshot-store/targets.test.ts src/cli/program/register.backup.test.ts src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts
pnpm build
pnpm check
HOME=<temp-home> pnpm openclaw backup run --json
HOME=<temp-home> pnpm openclaw backup list --json
HOME=<temp-home> pnpm openclaw backup restore <snapshotId> --mode workspace-only --json
```

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: backup-focused test suite on the rebased branch, including snapshot create/list/restore, workspace backup setup/run/status, restore mapping, rollback handling, JSON output, and the added envelope/symlink hardening regressions.
- Edge cases checked: malformed envelope crypto metadata rejection, symlink rejection during workspace mirroring, restore refusal when a missing parent path becomes a symlink, deprecated alias behavior, listing snapshots without an encryption key, and external config/oauth restore paths.
- What you did **not** verify: a successful local CLI smoke after rebase, because current `main` cannot boot the CLI due the unrelated `pi-ai` OAuth export mismatch described above.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps:
  - Existing users can keep using `backup create` / `backup push`, but the preferred commands are `backup export` / `backup run`.
  - To enable encrypted snapshots, set `backup.target` and `backup.encryption.key`.

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: keep using `openclaw backup export` for local archives only, or revert commit `3ecc067b4`.
- Files/config to restore: `openclaw.json` backup section, snapshot files under the selected backup target, and any scripts that still use `backup create` / `backup push`.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: `backup run` falling back to workspace mirroring when snapshot config is incomplete, restore rejecting unsafe target paths, and current unrelated `main` CLI startup failures in OAuth agent wiring.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: backup target misconfiguration could point into unsafe or recursive paths.
  - Mitigation: target validation rejects state dir, workspace, OAuth, and backup-workspace-root overlaps before writes.
- Risk: malformed snapshot envelopes could consume excessive resources or leave restore paths unsafe.
  - Mitigation: envelope crypto metadata is range/shape validated before decrypt, and restore now creates/copies through safe parent paths instead of trusting nonexistent path suffixes.
- Risk: alias compatibility could drift from the primary commands.
  - Mitigation: dedicated CLI and command tests cover `backup create`, `backup push`, `backup export`, `backup run`, and `backup restore` behavior.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
- `CI=true pnpm oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/send.ts extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts extensions/slack/src/blocks.test-helpers.ts`
- `CI=true pnpm vitest run extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts` (15 tests)
- `CI=true pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `git diff --check`

## Verification
- Thread-scoped progress chrome converts to `reactions.add` instead of `chat.postMessage`.
- Progress chrome without a reaction target is suppressed before Slack post.
- Semantic replies using the same leading emoji remain sendable.

target.title: feat: configure metadata (contextWindow, maxTokens, etc.) for custom provider setup
target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2-5 bullets: - Problem: `openclaw configure --section model` sets up providers and auth but never prompts for model metadata (contextWindow, maxTokens, reasoning, input types, cost). Users must hand-edit config or run many `config set` calls to configure these. - Why it matters: Custom/self-hosted endpoints default to contextWindow=16000 and maxTokens=4096, which are often wrong. target.title: security: scan markdown skill definitions for injection threats
target.body:
## Summary

The skill scanner (`src/security/skill-scanner.ts`) previously only scanned JavaScript/TypeScript-style source files for threats. This PR extends it to also scan Markdown `.md` files, including `SKILL.md` definitions, for injection and obfuscation patterns.

Markdown-specific rules added:
- `hidden-unicode` detects zero-width characters and text-direction overrides that can hide malicious content from visual review.
- `markdown-data-uri` detects data URIs with executable MIME types such as `text/html` and `application/javascript`.
- `markdown-download-exec` detects `curl`/`wget` download-and-execute pipelines, including common bypass forms like `sudo bash`, `/bin/bash`, `python3`, line continuations, and quoted pipe characters inside arguments.
- `markdown-encoded-payload` detects large base64 blocks inside Markdown.
- `markdown-hex-payload` detects hex-encoded payloads inside Markdown.

Implementation notes:
- Added `MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS` and `isMarkdown()`.
- Added `.md` to `SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS`.
- Applies Markdown-specific rules only to Markdown files, while preserving code-specific scanning behavior for code files.
- Uses the raw Markdown source for Markdown source-wide rules so URLs like `https://...` are not accidentally truncated by code-comment stripping.
- Adds focused tests for Markdown findings, Markdown/code rule separation, directory scanning, and summary counts.

Why this matters: skill definitions can include rendered Markdown. Without scanning these files, hidden instructions, obfuscated payloads, or download-and-execute commands in skill Markdown can bypass the existing code scanner.

Supersedes #10705 (auto-closed by stale bot). Rebased cleanly onto current `main`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 CHANGELOG.md src/security/skill-scanner.ts src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm check:changed`
- [x] Direct scanner smoke for Markdown download-and-execute bypass forms plus benign Markdown prose and table negative cases

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Markdown skill definitions such as `SKILL.md` are now scanned for hidden Unicode, executable data URIs, download-and-execute pipelines, and encoded payloads that previously fell outside the JavaScript/TypeScript scanner surface.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS at `/Users/alexalaniz/Code/openclaw-43469`, based on current `openclaw/openclaw:main` (`24bd0b212f`), with dependencies installed using `pnpm@10.33.2`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran the actual scanner through `node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs` against Markdown sources containing `curl`/`wget` bypass forms, then ran `pnpm test src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`, `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 CHANGELOG.md src/security/skill-scanner.ts src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`, and `pnpm check:changed`.

Evidence after fix: Copied live terminal output from the local OpenClaw checkout:

```text
markdown scanner smoke passed 7 positives and 2 negatives

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  32 passed (32)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.08s

All matched files use the correct format.

Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
runtime-sidecar-loaders: local runtime sidecar loaders look OK.
Import cycle check: 0 runtime value cycle(s).
```

Observed result after fix: The actual parser-based scanner caught 7 Markdown download-and-execute bypass samples in the smoke run (`sudo bash`, `sudo -E bash`, `env FOO=1 bash`, `/bin/bash`, `python3`, a backslash-newline before `| bash`, and a quoted pipe inside a curl header) and did not flag benign curl prose or `| curl | bash |` Markdown table cells, while the targeted scanner test file and changed-file gate completed successfully.

target.title: fix(skills): list omitted skill names when prompt is truncated
target.body:
## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

**Before:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit.
```

**After:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit. Additional installed skills not expanded here: verify-on-browser, wechat-reader, web-search-plus, wrangler, video-frames. If a listed skill name becomes relevant, inspect it with `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` before deciding whether to read its SKILL.md.
```

## Changes

- `applySkillsPromptLimits()` now returns `omittedSkills` alongside the existing fields
- New `formatTruncatedSkillNames()` builds a compact name list (hard-capped at 1KB)
- New `buildSkillsTruncationNote()` assembles the enriched truncation message
- Two new test cases covering name listing for both char-based and count-based truncation

## Tests

All 34 existing + new tests pass (`npx vitest run src/agents/skills`).

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

Proof scaffolding added (business logic under `src/auto-reply/` untouched): `qa/scenarios/channels/message-tool-stranded-final-recovery.md` (new scenario) and `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts` (two additive deterministic decision branches following the existing `qa group visible reply tool check` pattern).

Closes #85714







## Update — retry drain scheduling (follow-up)

Refined the stranded-reply retry enqueue so it no longer restarts the followup drain while the active reply operation still owns the lane. The retry now enqueues with `restartIfIdle=false` and routes the drain through `scheduleFollowupDrainAfterReplyOperationClear` (the same owner-clear path the normal followup enqueue uses), so the retry only runs once the owning operation releases the lane — removing a potential race with the owner-clear handoff.

- **Changed**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — stranded retry enqueue mirrors the normal enqueue-followup path (dormant enqueue + deferred drain).
- **Test**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — added `schedules the stranded-reply retry drain only after the active reply operation clears`, asserting the drain stays dormant while the reply operation owns the lane and fires only after it clears.

target.title: feat: add interactive launcher menu as thin wrapper over existing CLI
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users need a simple interactive menu to launch OpenClaw without remembering CLI commands. This PR adds a thin wrapper launcher that provides a friendly menu UX while delegating all operations to existing audited CLI commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher provides a single double-click entry point for common operations (TUI, WebUI, update, gateway management) without duplicating any existing OpenClaw surfaces. All sensitive operations remain in the existing audited code paths.

## User Impact

- **Interactive menu**: Run launcher to see TUI/WebUI/Update/Gateway options
- **No security risks**: Token handling remains in `openclaw dashboard`, no plaintext storage
- **No destructive operations**: Update delegates to `openclaw update` safe path
- **Proper service management**: Gateway uses `openclaw gateway install` (launchd/systemd/schtasks)

## Evidence

### Delegation Map
| Launcher Menu | Delegated To |
|--------------|--------------|
| [1] TUI | `openclaw tui` |
| [2] WebUI | `openclaw dashboard` |
| [3] Update | `openclaw update` |
| [4] Gateway | `openclaw gateway start/stop/restart/install` |

### What This PR Adds
- `launcher/src/main.rs` (347 lines) - Thin wrapper with interactive menu
- `launcher/README.md` - Documentation
- `launcher/Cargo.toml` - Rust project config
- `package.json` - Added `launcher:build` script

### What This PR Does NOT Do
- No plaintext token storage
- No custom git/pnpm operations
- No child-process gateway spawning
- No duplicate macOS packaging
- No custom updater logic

All operations delegate to existing canonical `openclaw` CLI commands.
