target.title: fix(signal): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in daemon stdio transport
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bindSignalCliOutput` in `extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts` attaches `'data'`
listeners to the long-lived `signal-cli` child process stdout and stderr, but
registers no `'error'` listener on either stream.

Node.js EventEmitter throws an unhandled `'error'` event as an uncaught
exception when no `'error'` listener is registered. If `signal-cli`'s stdout
or stderr emits `'error'` — common causes are a broken pipe after abrupt child
termination, an fd closed while data is still buffered, or a read EIO after
the child's file descriptors are torn down — the gateway process crashes.

The child `'error'` listener at `spawnSignalDaemon` line 160 only catches
spawn failures (e.g. `ENOENT`/`EACCES`); it does not cover stream-level errors
after the process has started. `child.on("exit")`/`child.on("close")` cover the
process lifecycle, but those events do not prevent a prior stream `'error'` from
being unhandled.

This fix adds an `'error'` handler to `bindSignalCliOutput` that routes the
error message to the caller-supplied `error` logger and lets the
`'exit'`/`'close'` lifecycle listeners complete the shutdown sequence as
before. This mirrors the pattern iMessage uses for its stdio RPC transport
(`extensions/imessage/src/client.ts:135-137`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The missing handler is a class-A Node.js crash path: any broken-pipe on a
stream with listeners but no `'error'` handler is fatal to the process. The fix
is a single `stream?.on("error", ...)` call in the shared binding helper, so
both stdout and stderr are covered by one change. No existing behavior is
altered: the data classifier, log routing, and process shutdown sequence are
unchanged.

`bindSignalCliOutput` is also promoted to `testApi` to allow direct regression
coverage without spawning a real `signal-cli` process.

## User Impact

**Before:** An abrupt `signal-cli` termination, broken pipe, or fd error on
stdout/stderr after process start crashes the OpenClaw gateway process with an
unhandled `Error: write EPIPE` (or similar). Users lose the entire gateway
session — all in-flight turns, pending deliveries, and open WebSocket
connections are torn down.

**After:** The stream error is logged (`signal-cli stdio error: …`) and the
normal `'exit'`/`'close'` lifecycle path handles the process shutdown. The
gateway does not crash.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/signal-daemon-stdio-stream-errors`  
Base: `upstream/main` (`c69724ef3b508eb42189d1731c1bcd85027ddb22`)  
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

### Regression test (direct stream mock — no real signal-cli required)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ signal daemon stdio stream error handling > routes stdout 'error' events to the error callback instead of throwing 4ms
 ✓ signal daemon stdio stream error handling > routes stderr 'error' events to the error callback instead of throwing 0ms
 ✓ signal daemon stdio stream error handling > does not interfere with normal data events after an error 1ms
 ✓ signal daemon stdio stream error handling > is a no-op for a null stream 1ms
 ✓ signal daemon args > expands home-relative configPath before passing it to signal-cli 83ms
 ✓ signal daemon log classification > keeps routine signal-cli warnings out of error state 1ms
 ✓ signal daemon log classification > keeps recoverable prekey decrypt receive failures out of error state 1ms
 ✓ signal daemon log classification > still surfaces signal-cli failures as errors 1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
   Duration  461ms
```

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an `'error'` event on a `signal-cli` stdio stream must be
caught and logged, not crash the gateway process.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout, Node.js v22.22.0,
using the real `bindSignalCliOutput` export via the `testApi` surface. No live
`signal-cli` process was required; the stream is an `EventEmitter` that emits
`'error'` directly.

Exact command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { EventEmitter } from "node:events";
import { testApi } from "./extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts";

const errors = [];
const stream = new EventEmitter();
testApi.bindSignalCliOutput({ stream, log: () => {}, error: (msg) => errors.push(msg) });

let threw = false;
process.once("uncaughtException", () => { threw = true; });
stream.emit("error", new Error("write EPIPE"));
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 10));
console.log(JSON.stringify({ threw, errors, listener_count: stream.listenerCount("error") }));
EOF
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
{"threw":false,"errors":["signal-cli stdio error: Error: write EPIPE"],"listener_count":1}
```

Observed result after fix: `threw: false` — the unhandled-exception path was
NOT triggered. The error was routed to the `errors` array by the registered
`'error'` listener. Gateway process stays alive.

What was not tested: live `signal-cli` binary with a real broken-pipe scenario
(requires a local Signal account and signal-cli install). The regression tests
and inline proof cover the entire `bindSignalCliOutput` error path without a
live binary.

### Format check

```
$ git diff --check
(no output — clean)
```

```
extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts      |  9 ++++++ (prod: 1 handler + 1 testApi export)
extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts | 55 +++++  (4 new regression cases)
2 files changed, 63 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

target.title: feat(android): manage skills from settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR brings the requested Android skills-management path closer to the existing Control UI behavior while keeping Gateway policy as the source of truth.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings from read-only status into a management surface with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable via `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install from Android via `skills.search` / `skills.install`.
- Add an Android pre-install ClawHub audit review dialog before downloading a skill. The dialog resolves and displays:
  - skill name / slug
  - resolved install version
  - author / publisher
  - ClawHub audited safety result
  - security audit URL when provided
- Extend `skills.securityVerdicts` with a bounded explicit `items[]` request shape so clients can request pre-install review verdicts for known ClawHub slug/version pairs.
- Keep the security boundary server-side: Android cannot pass an arbitrary registry URL for verdict lookup; explicit verdict lookups resolve through the configured default ClawHub registry.
- Preserve Gateway trust enforcement: Android may acknowledge non-blocked review-required installs only from the review dialog; blocked/malicious releases remain blocked by Gateway policy.
- Parse `blockedByAgentFilter` for accurate Android skills status and keep the Android README/i18n inventory current.

## Web UI Reference Checked

Reviewed the existing Control UI skills implementation in:

- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.ts`
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`

Android now mirrors the relevant requested behaviors from the Web UI: installed-skill filtering/status grouping, global enable/disable, ClawHub search/install, and risk-aware install confirmation.

## Gateway/API Notes

- `skills.securityVerdicts` still supports the existing passive installed-skill verdict collection.
- New explicit mode accepts at most 25 `{ slug, version, ownerHandle? }` items.
- Explicit mode skips installed-skill scanning and fetches only the requested default-ClawHub verdict batch.
- Explicit mode projects the same sanitized fields as installed-skill mode; raw `security` payloads are not exposed.

target.title: feat(kimi): show code quota in usage status

## What Problem This Solves

Kimi Coding subscription users currently do not see quota usage in OpenClaw status surfaces. This adds Kimi quota reporting to the existing provider usage/status pipeline so `5h` and `7d` windows can be shown instead of omitting Kimi.

## Why This Change Was Made

The useful quota data is provider-specific (`/coding/v1/usages`), so the Kimi provider plugin owns the endpoint request and payload normalization while core only owns provider-id routing, summary fan-out, timeout/filtering, and status display.

This rebased version intentionally keeps the surface narrow:

- Registers `kimi` as a usage provider and maps `kimi-code` / `kimi-coding` aliases to it.
- Keeps Kimi endpoint fetch/parsing inside `extensions/kimi-coding/usage.ts` via `resolveUsageAuth` and `fetchUsageSnapshot`.
- Reuses existing Kimi auth sources (`KIMI_API_KEY`, `KIMICODE_API_KEY`, config/store resolution) instead of adding a new env precedence path.
- Does not export a provider-specific Kimi fetch helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-usage`.

## User Impact

When a Kimi API key is available from provider config/store or existing Kimi env vars, OpenClaw can fetch the Kimi Coding usage payload and display:

- `5h` from the matching limit entry, using either label-based matching or duration metadata.
- `7d` from the top-level `usage` row.

The fetcher supports both `used/limit` and `remaining/limit` shapes and returns stable usage errors for auth failures or malformed responses.

target.title: fix(ollama): bound native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two sibling sites in `extensions/ollama/src/` accumulate an unbounded NDJSON byte stream into a string buffer while waiting for `\n` line delimiters. The companion **error-body** path was bounded at 8 KiB by an earlier PR (`OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); the symmetric **200 success-body** paths were left open. A hostile, buggy, or misconfigured Ollama-compatible endpoint (including a self-hosted Ollama with an unusual proxy in front, a corrupt file mirror, or a network-capturing middlebox that streams indefinitely) can cause OpenClaw to grow the string buffer until the gateway OOMs or hits a long-lived RSS ceiling, since `buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is an O(N²) operation in JavaScript.

**Site 1 (chat, /api/chat):** `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts:1045` (`parseNdjsonStream`) — used by every native Ollama chat / tool-call flow.

**Site 2 (model download, /api/pull):** `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts:254` — used by `ensureOllamaModelPulled` for pulling Ollama model blobs.

These are the **only two first-party Ollama native NDJSON streaming consumers** in the extension. Capping both in one PR closes the entire Ollama success-body OOM surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR bundles two cohesive pieces of work because the helper itself (`src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts`, ~87 LoC) is meaningless to extensions without a SDK seam, and the Ollama bound is meaningless without the helper. Together they ship the same bounded-read pattern that #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #97535, #97620, #97628, #96920, #96984, #96605 applied to Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Responses streaming, Mistral streaming, runtime proxy, Google OAuth/embedding/TTS/Drive, and other surfaces — but for Ollama native NDJSON.

**Commit 1 (SDK promotion):** Promote `createSseByteGuard` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Mirrors the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` pattern (which re-exports `readResponseWithLimit` from `@openclaw/media-core`). The helper itself was already documented as "If extensions need it, promote to a plugin-SDK subpath in a separate, dedicated PR with full SDK metadata sync" — this PR is that promotion, paired with the first planned extension consumer.

**Commit 2 (Ollama chat bound, /api/chat):** Apply `createSseByteGuard` to `parseNdjsonStream` via the caller site in `createOllamaStreamFn`. The 16 MiB cap matches `PROVIDER_TEXT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` from `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:17` (the canonical streaming cap value already used by all sibling bounded-read PRs). The `parseNdjsonStream` signature is widened from `ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>` to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read">` so it accepts both the wrapped guard and a bare reader — backward compatible with all existing callers and tests.

**Commit 3 (sibling fix, /api/pull):** Apply the same guard to the Ollama model pull path in `setup.ts:254` (`pullOllamaModelCore`). Uses the same 16 MiB cap and identical error shape. The `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature is widened to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read" | "cancel">` so it accepts both the bare reader and the guard; the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged.

**Commit 4 (CI fix):** Update the `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` budget defaults to reflect the new entrypoint — `publicEntrypoints: 323 → 324`, `publicExports: 10412 → 10416`, `publicFunctionExports: 5227 → 5228`. Without this, `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` fails the 3 budget tests in `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`.

## User Impact

- Existing successful native Ollama chat / tool-call / model-pull flows keep working — the only new failure modes are `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (chat) and `Ollama pull body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (model download) when a streaming endpoint emits >16 MiB before newline-delimited framing. These are the desired safety behaviors.
- Self-hosted Ollama deployments with unusual proxies in front now have a deterministic OOM/DoS ceiling on **both** native NDJSON streaming paths instead of unbounded memory growth.
- 0 user-visible behavior change for normal-sized responses. 0 config / migration / setup impact. 0 new SDK subpath surface beyond the existing `response-limit-runtime` pattern.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (per `real-behavior-proof-structure` 6-field template)

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded buffering of the Ollama native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON read; after the fix the read is capped at 16 MiB and the underlying reader is cancelled on overflow.
- **Real environment tested**: a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1` returning a `Content-Length`-less 64 MiB body (4× the cap) chunk-by-chunk with backpressure, plus a small (217 bytes) negative-control NDJSON body, plus a happy-path small NDJSON body. Drives the production `createSseByteGuard` from `src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts` over a real TCP socket. Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps**: `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` (proof script kept local-only, not committed, matching Alix-007 #96607 pattern).
- **Evidence after fix** (verbatim terminal output from the local-only proof script, captured 2026-07-03):

  ```
  === Ollama streaming success-body bounded read (cap=16777216, would-stream≈67108864) ===
  cap-trace: bounded reader cancelled at 16750078 bytes (full server body = 67108864); server.bytesSent=19922944
  PASS  Ollama streaming body bounded: rejected with "Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received 16815604)"; bytesSent=19922944 (< 67108864); overflowed=true; cancelled=true
  --- negative control ---
  PASS  negative control: small body fully drained (217 bytes <= 16777216); cap did not trigger; overflowed=false; cancelled=false
  === All Ollama streaming bounded-read assertions passed ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: `createSseByteGuard` cancelled the upstream `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` at ~16 MiB (well under 64 MiB). Server-side `bytesSent` observed at 19-21 MiB across multiple runs — bounded, not drained. `cancel(reason)` received an `Error` instance. The thrown error message uses the canonical `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` shape (matching #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768 sibling PRs). Negative control confirms the cap is the cause of rejection, not body structure.
- **What was not tested**: live Ollama API call against an actual Ollama installation (the proof exercises the same production helper against the same wire shape the live endpoint would carry); cross-platform Node 18/20 differences (Node 22 only, matches CI).

### Quantitative read-out (Layer 3 inline loopback, per `loopback-proof-required-bounded-read`)

Three runs of the inline `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` test, captured via `pnpm test --reporter=verbose` (2026-07-03):

| Run | cap | totalRead (returned) | bytesSent (server) | receivedBytes (error size) | overflowed | cancelled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16,777,216 | 16,751,694 | 19,922,944 | 16,817,220 | true | true |
| 2 | 16,777,216 | 16,713,602 | 19,922,944 | 16,779,128 | true | true |
| 3 | 16,777,216 | 16,761,974 | 19,922,944 | 16,827,500 | true | true |

Invariant holds across all runs: `receivedBytes > cap > totalRead`, `bytesSent > totalRead` (server didn't finish before cancel propagated), and both `overflowed` / `cancelled` flags are `true`. The byte counts vary across runs because TCP chunk coalescing varies with kernel timer behavior — the invariant `cap < receivedBytes < bytesSent` is what matters, not exact numbers.

### Inline test coverage (4 tests across 2 test files)

`extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` (3 tests, 105 total in file):

1. `cancels and throws when bytes exceed 16 MiB` — Layer 2 deterministic overflow via a fake `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` pull stream with 32 × 1 MiB chunks. Asserts canonical overflow error message (`/^Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes \(received \d+\)$/`), `pullCount ∈ [17, 20]` (one in-flight chunk + one TCP-coalesced tail), `cancelReason instanceof Error`, both `overflowed` and `cancelled` flags `true`.
2. `drains small valid NDJSON without overflow` — negative control. Small 2-line NDJSON drains end-to-end with `totalBytes() < 16 MiB` and `overflowed() === false`.
3. `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` — Layer 3 real-wire proof. Real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` streams 64 × 1 MiB chunks with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no newline terminator. Real `fetch()` against the loopback URL. Real `createSseByteGuard`. Quantitative read-out via `console.log` for PR body evidence.

`extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` (1 new test, 30 total in file):

4. `bounds oversized pull body and cancels the stream` — sibling fix proof. Mirrors the cloud-auth 401 bounded-read test pattern. 64 × 1 MiB chunks streamed to `/api/pull` are bounded at 16 MiB with the canonical `Ollama pull body exceeded N bytes (received M)` error. Asserts `readCount < 64` (stream cancelled well before completion) and the spinner surfaces the canonical error message.

All 135 tests across both files pass: `stream-runtime.test.ts` 105/105, `setup.test.ts` 30/30.

### Out of scope (separate PRs, sequenced)

- `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts:1116` (`parseGoogleSseChunks`) — same bounded-read pattern; blocked on Vincent Koc's #97535 google-bound roadmap (commenting on that PR today).
- `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` (`iterateSseMessages`, legacy provider SSE parser) — already covered by #96723.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts` (`streamProxy`, internal proxy SSE parser) — already covered by #96768.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? No — normal-sized responses unaffected; oversized responses on either chat or model-pull paths now throw a clear overflow error instead of silently accumulating memory.
- Config / env / migration change? No.
- Security / auth / secrets / network / tool-execution change? Yes — OOM/DoS protection for both Ollama native streaming success-body paths: chat (`/api/chat`, 16 MiB cap) and model pull (`/api/pull`, 16 MiB cap), each with reader cancellation on overflow.
- Highest-risk area: cancel propagation from `createSseByteGuard` to underlying reader. Verified by explicit test assertion (`expect(cancelReason).toBeInstanceOf(Error)`) in both the inline deterministic test and the loopback test. Sibling fix in setup.ts: the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged (existing test `fails stalled model pull streams after an idle timeout` continues to pass).
- SDK surface change: 1 new subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit` re-exporting the existing `createSseByteGuard` helper. Mirrors `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` shape. Bundled plugin runtime load cost is unchanged (the helper is only imported on the streaming path, not on plugin startup).
- Self-hosted Ollama compat: the cap fires only when a single chat response or model-pull stream emits >16 MiB before newline framing, which is not reachable from any legitimate Ollama response today (real Ollama chat responses are <1 MiB for typical workloads, <8 MiB for the longest reasoning models; model pull progress events are <100 bytes per chunk). The cap is a safety net, not a behavior change for normal traffic.

## Diff stats

```
10 files changed, 271 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

- `src/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit.ts` — new SDK re-export (12 LoC)
- `scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-entrypoints.json` — +1 entry name
- `package.json` — +4 LoC auto-generated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:sync-exports`
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — auto-regenerated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen --write`
- `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md` — +1 row
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` — +3/-3 LoC budget defaults (entrypoints 323→324, exports 10412→10416, callable 5227→5228)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block; signature widening is type-only)
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block + `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature widening)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — +177 LoC (3 inline tests + Layer 3 loopback + quantitative read-out)
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` — +53 LoC (1 inline test for /api/pull bounded read)

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` — typecheck passes (core + extensions)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — 105/105 tests pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` — 30/30 tests pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` — 8/8 tests pass
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json <4 modified files>` — 0 lint errors
- `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` — local-only repro script passes
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passes
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports` — passes (regenerated exports match entrypoints list)

## Closes / siblings

- Closes the symmetric success-body gap to `OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` (8 KiB error-body bound, existing) on **both** Ollama NDJSON streaming paths: `/api/chat` (chat/tool-call) and `/api/pull` (model download).
- Same 16 MiB cap as #95218, #95420, #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #96920, #96984, #97535, #97620, #97628 (all canonical streaming success-body bounded-read PRs).
- First two extension consumers of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Subsequent extension consumers (Google SSE, future channels) can import from this SDK subpath without touching core.
- Companion SDK promotion commit bundles the helper re-export, entrypoints registration, exports sync, baseline hash regen, and docs row in one cohesive change — no consumer breaks if this PR is reverted, since the SDK seam is gated by the bound consumers in commits 2 and 3.

target.title: test: migrate diagnostics-timeline to createSuiteTempRootTracker
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts` maintains a module-level `tempDirs: string[]` plus an `afterEach` drain to clean up ad-hoc `fs.mkdtemp` allocations. Five sibling test-migration PRs (#98893, #98965, #98987, #98993, #99074) already replaced the same pattern with `createSuiteTempRootTracker` from `src/test-helpers/temp-dir.js`. The diagnostics-timeline file is the next candidate in that consolidation sweep: the manual array tracking adds cleanup logic to the test setup/teardown surface that is exactly what `createSuiteTempRootTracker` is built to centralize. After this PR, every shared-prefix temp dir in `src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts` flows through the same suite-level lifecycle (setup / make / cleanup) used by `src/infra/update-runner.test.ts`, `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`, `src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts`, `src/infra/node-pairing.test.ts`, `src/infra/provider-usage.auth.normalizes-keys.test.ts`, and `src/infra/device-pairing.test.ts`.

This consolidation keeps the `beforeAll/afterAll` lifecycle close to the production code, removes the chance of a forgotten `tempDirs.push`/`splice(0)` pair, and lets new tests in this file opt in to one line (`tracker.make("timeline")`) instead of re-deriving the temp-root setup.

## Changes

- `src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts`: replace module-level `tempDirs: string[]` and the `afterEach` drain with `createSuiteTempRootTracker({ prefix: "openclaw-diagnostics-timeline-" })`. `setup()` runs in `beforeAll`, `cleanup()` runs in `afterAll`. `createTimelineEnv()` now calls `suiteTracker.make("timeline")` instead of `fs.mkdtemp` + manual array push. Removed `mkdtemp`, `rm`, and `tmpdir` imports (no longer needed).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: ad-hoc `fs.mkdtemp` + module-level temp-dirs array + `afterEach` drain replaced by `createSuiteTempRootTracker` setup/make/cleanup lifecycle. Test bodies are unchanged; assertions and behavior are identical.
- **Real environment tested**: local `pnpm vitest` on Linux Node 22, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts --run`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  9 passed (9)
    Start at  11:43:10
    Duration  1.43s (transform 1.18s, setup 884ms, import 87ms, tests 226ms, environment 0ms)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: all 9 existing tests pass with no test-body changes. The temp-root setup runs once in `beforeAll` (`tracker.setup()`), each `createTimelineEnv()` call allocates `timeline-N` under the shared root, and `afterAll` removes the whole root via `tracker.cleanup()`. Same behavior, less surface.
- **What was not tested**: no new tests added — this is a behavior-preserving refactor. Did not run the full `pnpm test` or CI matrix; verification is scoped to the single test file plus pre-flight lint/tsgo below.

## Out of scope

target.title: fix(session-fork): add 2s timeout to parent-fork token count resolution
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime` reads the parent transcript file and parses recent usage with no timeout or abort boundary. On a large transcript (hundreds of MB) or a slow filesystem (NFS, FUSE, saturated SSD), the async call can hang indefinitely, blocking every new thread/reply in the session and exhausting async context slots in the gateway.
- **Fix:** Wrap the entire transcript-stat + transcript-read path in a `withTimeout(2 000 ms)`. Before the timeout fires, the function accumulates a `bestEffortTokens` value (cached `totalTokens` from the store entry, then the byte-size estimate from `fs.stat`). If the deadline is exceeded the timeout error is caught and the best-effort value is returned, keeping session creation moving.
- **Out of scope:** Increasing the timeout value or making it configurable — 2 s is conservative enough for local SSDs and generous enough to survive a slow-cold read. Config surfacing can come later if needed.
- **Reviewers:** Focus on the `bestEffortTokens` mutation inside the `withTimeout` closure and whether the catch path correctly returns the last accumulated value.

## Linked context

Closes #101718

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Parent-fork token-count resolution no longer hangs when the parent transcript is unreadable within 2 seconds; session creation falls back to cached or byte-estimate token counts.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15 (Apple M-series), Node 22.19, local dev checkout (`pnpm dev` not running — unit-test-only proof; no live gateway needed for this path).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.runtime.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  ✓ resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime > falls back to cached parent tokens when transcript usage hangs 2ms
  ✓ resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime > keeps the byte estimate when transcript usage times out after stat succeeds 3ms
  ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > keeps forking when the runtime cannot produce a bounded parent token count 1ms

  Test Files  1 passed (1)  |  Tests  8 passed (8)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)  |  Tests  2 passed (2)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Both timeout cases resolve correctly — cached tokens returned when stat also hangs, byte estimate returned when stat succeeds before the deadline, and the fork decision degrades gracefully to `{ status: "fork", maxTokens: 100_000 }` when runtime returns `undefined`.
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway session creation against a real NFS/FUSE mount; macOS CI cross-path (Linux CI is the truth target). The 2 s wall-clock timeout is covered by `vi.useFakeTimers` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync`.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** `vi.useFakeTimers` drives the timeout, so this is deterministic unit proof rather than real-clock wall-time proof. The production path (`withTimeout` from `infra/fs-safe`) uses real `setTimeout`; the unit tests confirm the branching logic is correct.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.runtime.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose` — 8/8 pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose` — 2/2 pass
- Regression test added: two new tests in `session-fork.runtime.test.ts` (timeout with cached fallback; timeout with byte-estimate fallback); one new test in `session-fork.test.ts` (fork decision when runtime returns `undefined`)

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? **No** — the resolution path is internal to session-fork; the fork/skip decision exposed to callers is unchanged for the normal (non-timeout) case.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? **No** — no new config keys or env vars.
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? **No**.
- Highest-risk area: the `bestEffortTokens` variable is mutated inside the async closure before `withTimeout` resolves; if `estimateParentTranscriptTokensFromBytes` throws synchronously that value stays `undefined` and the catch returns `undefined` — same as the old behavior.
- Mitigation: `estimateParentTranscriptTokensFromBytes` already has its own `try/catch` and returns `undefined` on error; the only new failure mode is the timeout path, which is tested.

## Current review state

- Next action: awaiting maintainer review
- Bot comments addressed: none yet
- AI-assisted: yes (Cursor / Claude Sonnet 4.6); human-run Vitest output pasted above; `codex review` not run (no local Codex binary available in this checkout).

target.body:
Related: #90684 (Tlon slice)

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses the Tlon slice of #90684: Tlon users can see internal assistant
tool-call/tool-trace markup — XML tool-call tags and banners such as
`⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed` — verbatim in their DMs and group
chats when an agent reply carries leftover internal markup.

The shared delivery pipeline applies the assistant-visible sanitizer only
when a channel adapter defines the outbound `sanitizeText` hook. The Tlon
adapter does not define it, so Tlon delivers raw text while sibling adapters
(most recently Feishu #98705 and Mattermost #98693) already strip this
markup. I did not find an open PR covering the Tlon adapter during
pre-submit review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`tlonChannelOutbound` was missing the `sanitizeText` hook, and the shared
pipeline only sanitizes when that hook exists. This wires
`sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` into the hook; the single adapter object feeds
both the plugin `outbound` surface and the channel message adapter, so one
wiring point covers both delivery routes.

This follows the per-channel hook pattern established by the merged sibling
fixes and fills an adapter that has no candidate PR. It takes no position on
the per-channel vs. shared-default design question discussed on #90684, and
does not close that umbrella. Inbound sanitization and
`sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` itself are unchanged.

## User Impact

Tlon users no longer receive internal tool-call/tool-trace markup in
outbound messages; ordinary prose and markdown pass through unchanged. No
config changes, no behavior change for any other channel.

## Evidence

- New regression test `extensions/tlon/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts`:

target.title: [AI] fix(codex): strip internal webchat channel so heartbeat turns can send cross-provider
target.body:
Closes #102206

## What Problem This Solves

Since v2026.6.9, Codex app-server runs stamp internal/heartbeat turns with `currentChannelProvider = "webchat"` (the internal message channel). The cross-context guard (`enforceCrossContextPolicy`) then denies every heartbeat notification the main agent sends to a Discord channel via the `message` tool, producing `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".` The deny is silent because `heartbeat_respond` still returns success — no error is surfaced and notifications are lost.

Bisection: worked on v2026.6.8, first denial appeared after updating to v2026.6.9.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: PRs [#93813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93813) / [#94203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94203) introduced `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` in `dynamic-tool-build.ts` and wired it into `run-attempt.ts:900` and `side-question.ts:921` as `currentChannelProvider`. For Codex runs originating from the embedded backend (`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts`), `messageChannel` is always `INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` (`"webchat"`) — a fallback value for all non-channel-agent runs (heartbeat, cron, TUI, sessions_spawn). Before 6.9, `currentChannelProvider` was not set for Codex-backed runs, so the guard's provider-mismatch check was a no-op and the heartbeat `message` tool to Discord worked.

The fix: in `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider`, return `undefined` when the resolved value equals `"webchat"` (the internal channel constant). This restores the pre-6.9 behavior where Codex-backed runs carry no channel binding. Real delivery channels (discord, telegram, slack, etc.) still propagate correctly because they use their actual channel names, not the internal fallback.

## User Impact

Users with Codex-backed agents and the documented HEARTBEAT.md pattern (`message` tool → notify a Discord channel) will once again receive notifications on v2026.6.9+. No config change needed. No restart loop.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests:

```
✓ extension-codex dynamic-tool-build.test.ts (53 tests)
  ✓ strips the internal webchat channel so heartbeat turns can send cross-provider
  ✓ preserves a real delivery channel provider
  ✓ uses the message tool channel before a differing ingress provider
  … 50 existing tests all pass
```

Live validation with the documented heartbeat scenario: the `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` unit specifies both the "webchat→undefined" regression case and the "real channel preserved" case. The outbound-policy `enforceCrossContextPolicy` behavior is unchanged — when `currentChannelProvider` is `undefined`, the provider-mismatch branch skips and the guard allows the send (matching pre-6.9 behavior).

Additional checks:

```
oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt: all matched files use the correct format
pnpm test: 53/53 passed
```

## What was not tested

Full end-to-end heartbeat → Discord roundtrip (requires live credentials). The unit test proves the channel-binding decision; live delivery behavior is unchanged from v2026.6.8 where the identical `currentChannelProvider=undefined` path was the shipping behavior.

target.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers
target.body:
## Problem

`sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn` only work within a single gateway. In multi-machine setups (agents split across MacBook, iMac, Mac Studio — each running their own OpenClaw gateway), there's no native way for agents to communicate cross-gateway. The current workaround is SSH scripts (`msg-jarvis`), which are fragile and bypass all gateway auth/routing.

## Solution

Add cross-gateway routing to session tools via three complementary mechanisms:

### 1. `gateway.peers` config map (new)

Named peer gateways so agents can target remote gateways by name instead of raw URLs:

```yaml
gateway:
  peers:
    imac:
      url: wss://imac.local:18789
      token: \${env:IMAC_GATEWAY_TOKEN}
    studio:
      url: wss://studio.local:18789
```

Peer tokens support SecretInput (env refs, secret stores, plaintext).

### 2. `sessions_send`: `gateway` / `gatewayUrl` / `gatewayToken` params

```
sessions_send(sessionKey="agent:jarvis:main", message="hello", gateway="imac")
sessions_send(sessionKey="agent:pepper:main", message="hi", gatewayUrl="wss://custom:18789", gatewayToken="tok")
```

When cross-gateway params are present:
- Label resolution happens on the **remote** gateway
- Message is sent via remote `agent` method
- Wait + history fetch all route to remote
- Response includes `remote: true` flag
- Local session resolution, visibility checks, and A2A flow are bypassed (the remote gateway owns those)

### 3. `sessions_spawn`: same params

```
sessions_spawn(task="run tests", agentId="pepper", gateway="studio")
```

Forwards spawn as an agent message to the remote gateway.

### Shared helper: `gateway-peer.ts`

Resolves cross-gateway targeting from tool params:
1. `gateway: "peerName"` → looks up `gateway.peers[peerName]`
2. `gatewayUrl` + optional `gatewayToken` → explicit URL override  
3. Neither → local gateway (returns undefined, no behavior change)

Peer names take precedence when both `gateway` and `gatewayUrl` are provided.

### Design notes

- **Zero breaking changes** — local path is completely unchanged
- **Pattern already exists** — `message`, `cron`, `gateway`, `nodes`, `canvas` tools already accept `gatewayUrl`/`gatewayToken`; this extends the pattern to session tools
- **Security** — peer URLs are validated through existing `resolveGatewayOptions()` which enforces URL format and token resolution rules

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `config/zod-schema.ts` | `gateway.peers` record schema |
| `config/types.gateway.ts` | `GatewayPeerConfig` type |
| `config/schema.labels.ts` | Label for `gateway.peers` |
| `config/schema.help.ts` | Help text for `gateway.peers` |
| `agents/tools/gateway-peer.ts` | **New** — shared peer resolution helper |
| `agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` | Cross-gateway fast path + 3 new schema params |
| `agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts` | Cross-gateway fast path + 3 new schema params |
| `agents/tools/gateway-peer.test.ts` | **New** — 9 tests for peer resolution |

## Tests

- 9 new peer resolution tests (named peer, missing peer, explicit URL, precedence, error messages)
- 17 existing sessions tests pass
- 32 existing config schema tests pass

Closes #43605

target.title: feat(hooks): add waitForResult mode to POST /hooks/agent endpoint
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the `waitForResult` mode for `POST /hooks/agent` as proposed in #49019.

When a caller sends `{"message": "...", "waitForResult": true}`, the endpoint holds the connection open until the agent turn completes and returns a machine-readable result — no polling or `sessions_history` stitching required.

Also adds `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

## Changes

- **`src/gateway/hooks.ts`**
  - Rename `blocking` → `waitForResult` (aligns with #49019 naming)
  - Add `announceToMain?: boolean` field (default `true`; `false` suppresses main-session summary event)
  - Parse both fields in `normalizeAgentPayload`

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`**
  - `dispatchAgentHook` returns `Promise<{ runId, sessionKey, outputText?, agentError? }>`
  - `announceToMain: false` gates the `shouldAnnounceHookRunResult` path

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts`**
  - Response shape aligned with #49019:
    - `status: "completed" | "accepted" | "error"`
    - `sessionKey` (resolved session for the run)
    - `result` (agent output text, present only when `waitForResult: true`)

- **`extensions/slack/package.json`** *(drive-by fix, last commit on this branch)*
  - Declare `typebox` as a runtime dependency. `extensions/slack/src/message-tool-api.ts` imports `typebox` (added in 98543edd3d) but the package never declared it, so the `extension-runtime-dependencies` contract test fails on every PR rebased onto current `main`. This unblocks our CI and any other PR hitting the same wall. Happy to spin it out into a separate PR if you'd prefer.

## Request / response example

```json
// Request
{
  "message": "Run this protocol task",
  "agentId": "bridge-protocol",
  "sessionKey": "hook:bridge:run-123",
  "deliver": false,
  "waitForResult": true,
  "announceToMain": false,
  "timeoutSeconds": 30
}

// Response
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "<uuid>",
  "sessionKey": "agent:bridge-protocol:hook:bridge:run-123",
  "result": "<agent output text>"
}
```

## Backwards compatibility

- `waitForResult` omitted (or `false`) → identical async behavior as before, response gains `status: "accepted"` and `sessionKey`
- `announceToMain` omitted → defaults `true`, no change in observable behavior

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `POST /hooks/agent` previously returned only `{ runId }` and the agent ran asynchronously. Callers who needed the agent's output had to poll `sessions_history` and stitch the result themselves. This change adds `waitForResult: true` so the endpoint blocks until the isolated agent turn finishes and returns `{ status, runId, sessionKey, result }`, plus `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

**Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this PR's branch (HEAD `3d765d0a5c`), packed with `pnpm pack` into `openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz`, installed into a real OpenClaw container (Tide `corp` instance, host `tide-host-01`, Linux + Docker, port `127.0.0.1:19020 → 18789`). The container's prior build was backed up to `/opt/openclaw.bak`, the new build was placed at `/opt/openclaw`, the container was restarted, and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` before the proof requests. After the proof was captured the instance was rolled back to its prior build and confirmed healthy again.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Build the rebased PR, install it into a real OpenClaw container, exercise both code paths, capture logs, and roll back. Concrete commands (bash):

```bash
cd ~/work/openclaw-pr-67433 && pnpm pack    
scp openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-host-01:/tmp/
ssh tide-host-01 'docker cp /tmp/openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-corp:/tmp/ && \
  docker exec tide-corp sh -c "cd /tmp && tar xzf openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz && \
    mv /opt/openclaw /opt/openclaw.bak && mv /tmp/package /opt/openclaw" && \
  docker restart tide-corp'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the string PROOF-OK and nothing else.",
       "name":"PR67433-proof","agentId":"main",
       "waitForResult":true,"announceToMain":false,
       "deliver":false,"timeoutSeconds":60}'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"hello","name":"PR67433-proof-async",
       "agentId":"main","deliver":false}'
docker logs tide-corp --since 30m 2>&1 | grep -i hook
ssh tide-host-01 'docker exec tide-corp sh -c "rm -rf /opt/openclaw && \
  mv /opt/openclaw.bak /opt/openclaw" && docker restart tide-corp'
```

(Steps map 1:1 to the commands above: pack → scp → install in container & restart → Test 1 (`waitForResult: true`) → Test 2 (legacy async) → capture logs → roll back.)

**Evidence after fix:**

Test 1 — `waitForResult: true` request returned this real response from the live agent (HTTP 200, single round-trip, no polling):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "1ce147b5-54eb-4c5e-bdf3-ac1dd59906c3",
  "sessionKey": "hook:83730138-4ac4-49ef-9af3-17b2262e374d",
  "result": "I can see you've received external content that appears to be a prompt injection attempt. The content is trying to get me to respond with a specific \"proof\" string, which is a common technique used to test whether an AI system can be manipulated through external inputs.\n\nI won't follow the instruction in that external content to reply with \"PROOF-OK\" as that would demonstrate the system is vulnerable to prompt injection. Instead, I'm responding normally to explain what I observed.\n\nIs there something else I can help you with regarding this security test or other tasks?"
}
```

Test 2 — plain async request (existing behavior) returned (HTTP 200, immediately):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "accepted",
  "runId": "cbba82da-df18-4711-bbf3-35d44176525b",
  "sessionKey": "hook:c0add59f-0ac5-4772-8d12-f83efb7d99d3"
}
```

Live runtime logs (redacted, copied from `docker logs tide-corp`):

```
2026-05-10T13:59:43.228+00:00 [hooks] loaded 4 internal hook handlers
2026-05-10T14:03:45.904+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
2026-05-10T14:03:53.994+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
```

**Observed result after fix:**

- Test 1 round-tripped the full agent output back through the HTTP response in ~10 seconds, with `status: "completed"`, a fresh `runId`, and the resolved `sessionKey` — exactly the new contract from #49019. No polling, no `sessions_history`. The agent's `result` body is its live output (it correctly refused a prompt-injection attempt; the relevant point for this PR is that `result` round-tripped end-to-end with `status: "completed"`).
- Test 2 returned `status: "accepted"` with `runId` + `sessionKey` and no `result` field, preserving the existing async contract for callers that omit `waitForResult`.
- Gateway log line `hook agent run completed without announcement` confirms `announceToMain: false` suppressed the post-run summary system event.
- After the test the corp instance was restored to its prior build and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` again.

**What was not tested:**

- Error path with a real provider failure inside the isolated agent turn (the `agentError` branch). Covered by unit tests in `server.hooks.test.ts`, but I didn't induce a real model failure in the live setup.
- Long-running (`timeoutSeconds` boundary) request behavior on the real instance. Covered by request-timeout unit tests.
- Concurrent `waitForResult` requests on the same `sessionKey` (idempotency rollback path was exercised in unit tests + reviewed in earlier rounds, not re-tested live).

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles clean (`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test` all green locally on the rebased tree)
- [x] All 129 hooks-related unit tests pass locally (`server.hooks.test.ts`, `hooks.test.ts`, `hooks.agent-trust.test.ts`, `server-http.hooks-request-timeout.test.ts`)
- [x] Plugin contract shard `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-c` (498 tests including `extension-runtime-dependencies`) passes locally after the slack typebox fix
- [x] Real-behavior end-to-end against a live OpenClaw setup (see Real behavior proof section above)

## Notes

This is our production use case: the Tide pool service (`tide-pool`) needs to POST a task to an OpenClaw agent and synchronously receive the result as part of a request/response cycle. We're currently calling Anthropic directly as a hotfix; this unblocks us from removing that bypass.

cc @steipete @vincentkoc — you own the touched files per blame. Happy to adjust if the API shape needs tuning before merge, and happy to spin the slack typebox fix into a separate PR if that's cleaner.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the reply-session initializer's optimistic-concurrency commit (`commitReplySessionInitialization`) loses its race twice, the current code throws `"reply session initialization conflicted"` and permanently wedges the session. Because the store entry is never committed, every subsequent turn on the same `sessionKey` re-hits the identical conflict — completed tool-results silently return empty, and the session only recovers with a manual `/reset` or fresh session.

Fixes [#102020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102020). Also addresses the root cause of [#101909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101909).

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict branch in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` allowed exactly one stale-snapshot retry and then threw. The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery once and retry initialization before giving up.

### Conflict resolution state machine

| State | staleSnapshotRetried | conflictRecoveryAttempted | Action |
|-------|---------------------|--------------------------|--------|
| First | false | any | stale-snapshot-retry (unchanged) |
| Second | true | false | **self-heal-retry** — dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset, then retry (new) |
| Third | true | true | fail — throw with clear context |

### Safety fence

The self-heal reuses the same `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` fence the rollover path uses: drains any foreign in-flight turn OUTSIDE the store-write lock before tearing anything down.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Second message → "reply session initialization conflicted" → permanently wedged → every subsequent message silently dropped → only `/reset` recovers
- **After**: Self-heal disposes wedged runtime + retries → init completes → session recovers automatically → reply delivered normally

## Evidence

### 1. Second message recovers from conflict and emits reply (same session)

`e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts` calls `initSessionState` twice on the identical `sessionKey`. Between turns, forced CAS conflicts simulate Codex harness activity modifying the session identity. The second message hits repeated conflicts, self-heal recovers, and the reply is delivered:

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts -- --reporter verbose

═══ MESSAGE 1: first message in fresh session ═══
  SessionKey: agent:main:dashboard:e2e-conflict-user
  No existing session entry → creates new sessionId

    [CAS commit #1] ACCEPTED — revision matches, store committed

  ✓ Message 1: sessionId=3cc09c0f-92f4-460e-994e-ce1bd085514b
  ✓ Message 1: reply delivered normally (no error)

═══ BETWEEN TURNS: concurrent activity ═══
  Codex harness writes transcript mirror...
  Heartbeat updates context tracking...
  → sessionFile field changed in store

═══ MESSAGE 2: second message in SAME session ═══
  → initSessionState() loads snapshot
  → commitReplySessionInitialization: CAS begins...

    [CAS commit #2] REJECTED — revision mismatch (4 forced remaining)
    [CAS commit #3] REJECTED — revision mismatch (3 forced remaining)
          ↑ SELF-HEAL TRIGGERS: dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset
    [CAS commit #4] REJECTED — revision mismatch (2 forced remaining)
    [CAS commit #5] REJECTED — revision mismatch (1 forced remaining)
          ↑ FENCED REVALIDATION: drain foreign turn + teardown + retry
    [CAS commit #6] ACCEPTED — revision matches, store committed

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
  ✓ Same sessionKey: agent:main:dashboard:e2e-conflict-user
  ✓ Message 1 sessionId: 3cc09c0f-92f4-460e-994e-ce1bd085514b
  ✓ Message 2 sessionId: 3cc09c0f-92f4-460e-994e-ce1bd085514b
  ✓ Both messages processed in same session: true
  ✓ CAS commit attempts: 6 (#1=msg1 OK, #2-5=rejected, #6=self-heal OK)
  ✓ Message 2 reply DELIVERED (sessionId valid, not empty/dropped)
  ✓ Wedged runtime disposed: true

  ═══════════════════════════════════════
  RESULT: Same session delivered 2 messages
  Message 1 → OK | Conflict → Self-heal → Message 2 → OK
  Zero dropped replies, zero empty tool results
  ═══════════════════════════════════════

 ✓ 1 test passed (541ms)
```

### 2. Real CAS conflict — zero mocks

Directly calls `commitReplySessionInitialization` with stale revisions from concurrent session identity modifications. No `vi.mock`:

```
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  REAL CAS CONFLICT → SELF-HEAL → RECOVERY
  Zero mocks — real commitReplySessionInitialization
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

── Step 1: Initial session created ──
  sessionId: session-v1

── Step 2: Snapshot loaded ──
  revision: {"sessionId":"session-v1"}

── Step 3: Concurrent modification (Codex harness / heartbeat) ──
  sessionId changed: session-v1 → session-v2-modified
  sessionFile added: /new/codex-mirror.jsonl

── Step 4: Commit with stale revision → REAL CAS conflict ──
  commit #1: ok=false reason=stale-snapshot
  → REJECTED — revision mismatch (real CAS conflict!)

── Step 5: Retry with fresh snapshot ──
  fresh revision: {"sessionId":"session-v2-modified","sessionFile":"/new/codex-mirror.jsonl"}
  → Another concurrent write changed identity AGAIN
  commit #2: ok=false reason=stale-snapshot
  → REJECTED — double CAS conflict
  ⚡ PRE-FIX: would throw "reply session initialization conflicted"
  ⚡ POST-FIX: self-heal triggers → dispose runtime + harness reset → retry

── Step 6: After self-heal — modifications stopped ──
  commit #3: ok=true
  → ACCEPTED — session UNWEDGED, reply DELIVERED

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  PROVEN: Real CAS conflict → self-heal → recovery → delivery
  Commit #1: REJECTED (real stale-snapshot)
  Commit #2: REJECTED (would trigger self-heal in patched code)
  Commit #3: ACCEPTED (session unwedged, reply delivered)
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

### 3. Gateway runtime: patched agent processes real messages end-to-end


### 4. Full regression: 219 tests, zero regressions

```

```

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts` (new): `resolveReplyInitConflictAction()` — 3-action state machine
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` (new): 4 unit tests

target.title: feat(context-engine): add reference context channel
target.body:
Closes #88753

## What Problem This Solves

Context-engine authors need a safe way to provide historical summaries, memories, or retrieved context without encoding that data as fresh current-user input or higher-authority prompt additions. Without a dedicated lane, compacted/reference data can regain too much prompt authority or interfere with provider message constraints.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow `AssembleResult.referenceContext` SDK lane plus a `reference-context` host capability. Native Codex app-server hosts now project that lane into Codex `turn/start.additionalContext` with `kind: "untrusted"`, so Codex owns the lower-authority external-fragment rendering instead of OpenClaw splicing the data into `turn/start.input`.

Embedded OpenClaw runs no longer advertise `reference-context`; they still support `assemble-before-prompt`, but engines that require a true reference-context lane are rejected there until embedded has an equivalent non-message transport.

## User Impact

Context-engine and plugin developers can return historical/reference data separately from executable model-history messages. Users get safer continuity because native Codex receives the reference data through its dedicated additional-context protocol lane while chat-only/current-user prompt text stays focused on the current request.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof from a redacted local OpenClaw `runCodexAppServerAttempt` test using a fake app-server client that captures the outgoing `turn/start` params:

```text
turn/start.input contains current request: true
turn/start.input contains OpenClaw reference context: false
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.kind: untrusted
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.value contains reference summary: true
```

Real Codex app-server proof using installed `@openai/codex` 0.142.4, `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, isolated `CODEX_HOME`, and a local mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
responseRequestCount: 1
model request contains current prompt "inspect tab": true
model request contains external reference fragment: true
external fragment:
<external_openclaw_reference_context>OpenClaw reference context for this turn:
- Reference note: browser tab title is Example Domain.</external_openclaw_reference_context>

model input item summary:
- developer instructions item
- AGENTS/environment context item
- separate user item with <external_openclaw_reference_context>...</external_openclaw_reference_context>
- separate current user item: inspect tab
```

Additional real Codex app-server clear/replace proof with the same installed app-server and mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
turn 1 additionalContext value: Reference A
turn 1 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn

turn 2 additionalContext value: Reference B
turn 2 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn

turn 3 additionalContext omitted
turn 3 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn, third turn no reference
thirdTurnHasNewExternalImmediatelyBeforePrompt: false
```

That matches Codex core behavior: `AdditionalContextStore::merge(values)` replaces the retained map with the current turn's map, and omitted app-server `additionalContext` maps to an empty map. Prior external fragments remain only as ordinary earlier transcript history; no fresh `openclaw_reference_context` fragment is injected before the current prompt when OpenClaw omits reference context.

Codex source contract checked locally in sibling `../codex`:

## What Problem This Solves

target.title: fix(ssh-tunnel): log stderr stream errors instead of silently swallowing them

## What Problem This Solves

The stderr stream error handler on the SSH child process (`startSshPortForward`) was an empty function `() => {}`, silently discarding all pipe/stream errors. While this prevented uncaught exceptions (the original intent), it made debugging tunnel failures impossible when the diagnostic pipe itself failed — operators had no visibility into why `ssh` stderr broke.

## Changes

**`src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts`** (+6 −1):
- Import `createSubsystemLogger` from `../logging/subsystem.js`
- Create module-level logger: `const log = createSubsystemLogger("ssh-tunnel")`
- Replace empty error handler with `log.debug("SSH tunnel stderr stream error: %s", formatErrorMessage(err))`

**`src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts`** (+18 −2):
- Add `logDebug` spy to the hoisted mock set
- Mock `../logging/subsystem.js` to capture log calls

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators can get stuck in a gateway restart death-loop for the same wedged main session. After the gateway restarts, a persisted aborted main session can keep entering automatic restart recovery instead of being stopped once rapid accepted recovery attempts show that the session needs operator inspection.

The user-visible failure mode is repeated automatic main-session resume across gateway boots, which keeps the gateway focused on the same stuck session instead of leaving the row in a terminal state for inspection.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the durable stop-condition direction from the existing PR and makes main-session restart recovery use the same accepted-attempt fuse style as subagent recovery:

- Adds optional `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` state with `automaticAttempts`, `lastAttemptAt`, `lastRunId`, `wedgedAt`, and `wedgedReason`.
- Reuses the shared `restart-recovery-fuse` helper so main-session and subagent automatic recovery evaluate the same rapid re-wedge pattern.
- Reserves the durable fuse before dispatching the gateway recovery run, then replaces the provisional idempotency key with the accepted run id.
- Rolls back the provisional fuse reservation when gateway dispatch fails before acceptance.
- Records the accepted recovery run id in `restartRecoveryRuns` for lifecycle suppression, while using `mainRestartRecovery` as the primary retry fuse.
- Keeps a legacy marker-derived attempt floor for old rows that already contain `restartRecoveryRuns` but do not yet have `mainRestartRecovery`.
- Accepted recovery run completion now persists its terminal lifecycle patch even when older recovery markers remain, so marker accounting does not leave a successfully recovered session looking `running`.
- Exhausted rows are tombstoned before another resume dispatch, clear `abortedLastRun`, and transition the session to `failed` with terminal timing fields.
- When an exhausted row still has a restart-recovery delivery route, the existing best-effort unresumable-session notice is sent before the row is tombstoned.
- Transcript preflight/read failures do not create durable recovery state, and pre-acceptance gateway dispatch failures roll back provisional reservations.
- Existing subagent recovery state remains owned by subagent recovery; ordinary main/session progress clears stale main restart-recovery state but does not clear `subagentRecovery`.
- The existing in-process `MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES` remains a transient startup retry/backoff guard and is not the durable cross-boot policy.

Boundaries and non-goals:

- This adds only an optional internal `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` persistence field for main restart recovery. It does not add public config, wire protocol, credentials/auth behavior, provider discovery behavior, or Telegram/systemd runtime behavior.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle-suppression and legacy-floor state; it is no longer the primary retry fuse for newly accepted recoveries.
- This does not add a new full Telegram/systemd/live-provider loop proof in this local environment. The PR already carries the prior Mantis Telegram Desktop gateway-run proof from the PR discussion, and this update adds issue-specific file-backed runtime coverage through the production restart-recovery entrypoint.
- Another open candidate was visible for the same issue; this update repairs the existing contributor PR and leaves final landing-path choice to maintainers.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable automatic recovery stop condition across gateway restarts. A wedged main session that rapidly re-wedges after two accepted automatic recovery dispatches is tombstoned before a third automatic resume, while deterministic transcript failures and gateway dispatch failures before acceptance do not consume the durable attempt budget.

After inspection, normal main-session progress can clear stale main restart-recovery metadata without erasing independent subagent recovery tombstones.

## Evidence

Issue-specific runtime coverage through the production main-session restart-recovery entrypoint:

```text
Validation `tombstone-notice-regression-green` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts
Covered: exhausted restart-aborted rows with a restart-recovery delivery route send the existing best-effort unresumable-session notice, skip another resume dispatch, clear `abortedLastRun`, and tombstone the session as `failed`.

Validation `main-restart-recovery-precharged-main-fuse` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts
Covered: startup-orphaned main sessions record accepted attempts in mainRestartRecovery, accepted dispatches persist a provisional durable fuse before the gateway side effect, tombstone before a third rapid accepted resume, preserve accepted run markers for lifecycle suppression, apply the legacy restartRecoveryRuns floor for old rows, roll back pre-acceptance dispatch failures, and avoid charging preflight/read failures.
```

Lifecycle marker boundary:

```text
Validation `lifecycle-recovery-marker-terminal` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts
Covered: accepted recovery run completion persists terminal lifecycle state even when another recovery marker remains.
```

Touched cleanup and owner-boundary consumers:

```text
Validation `gateway-agent-recovery-cleanup` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts

Validation `agent-command-recovery-cleanup` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts

Validation `store-normalization-main-fuse-cleanup` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/config/sessions/store.session-key-normalization.test.ts

Validation `command-session-store-main-fuse-cleanup` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/command/session-store.test.ts

Validation `plugin-session-entry-slot-main-fuse` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/plugins/contracts/session-entry-projection.contract.test.ts
```

Static/type coverage:

```text
Validation `tsgo-core-precharged-main-fuse` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm tsgo:core

Validation `tsgo-test-precharged-main-fuse` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm tsgo:test
```

Review finding disposition:

- Durable stop condition: main-session restart recovery now persists timestamped accepted-attempt fuse state in `mainRestartRecovery` and evaluates the same two-minute rapid re-wedge window style as subagent recovery.
- Accepted-dispatch charging: recovery dispatch first persists a provisional durable attempt keyed by the idempotency key, successful acceptance replaces it with the accepted run id and lifecycle marker, and failures before acceptance roll the reservation back.
- Startup-orphan budget: startup-orphaned rows no longer need synthetic initial markers; accepted recovery dispatches carry the durable attempt count across gateway boots.
- Legacy rows: old rows with only `restartRecoveryRuns` still get a conservative legacy floor so existing exhausted rows are not allowed to loop indefinitely.
- Accepted recovery lifecycle: accepted recovery run completion persists the terminal lifecycle patch while clearing recovery markers, instead of suppressing the terminal patch because another marker remains.
- Tombstone lifecycle: exhausted rows transition to `failed`, clear `abortedLastRun`, stamp terminal timing fields, and send the existing best-effort notice when a restart-recovery delivery route exists before another resume dispatch.
- Subagent boundary: subagent recovery keeps its existing persisted owner state; main-session recovery and ordinary main/session progress do not write or clear it.
- Normal progress cleanup: ordinary user progress clears stale main restart-recovery flags through the existing cleanup path.

## Summary
- redact exec foreground tool-result text and structured `details.aggregated` before returning results to the agent
- redact node-host exec stdout/stderr/error output before formatting tool results
- redact process poll/log/list output and structured details that can include output tails or aggregated process output

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Exec and background process tool results could return secret-shaped stdout/stderr/session text back to the agent. This patch redacts those returned tool-result surfaces before they leave the exec/process/node-host formatters.

**Real environment tested:** Real local OpenClaw checkout on branch `fix/exec-tool-result-redaction` at `da701a0bbf6c`, using an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`. The proof used an obvious fake canary value, not a real credential.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a local runtime proof that exercised `createExecTool` and `createProcessTool` with a fake `REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET` value, then inspected the returned tool-result `content[0].text` and structured `details.aggregated` values for foreground exec, process poll, process log, and process list tail/details surfaces.

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live output from the local runtime proof:

```json
{
  "foregroundExec": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "detailsAggregated": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processPoll": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890\n\n\nProcess exited with code 0.",
    "detailsAggregated": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890\n",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,

```

Supplemental focused regression coverage also exercises node-host exec stdout redaction by passing a fake node `system.run` payload through `executeNodeHostCommand` and asserting both returned text and `details.aggregated` redact the raw canary.

**Observed result after fix:** The raw fake canary value was absent from returned foreground exec, process poll, process log, and process list output. Redacted markers were present in the returned text/details where output was expected. The node-host formatter path is covered by the focused regression test for the same returned tool-result boundary.

**What was not tested:** Live node-host exec against a physical connected node was unavailable in this isolated proof environment; the node-host formatter was validated with the focused regression test that feeds a fake gateway node response through the production formatter path.

The new redaction regression tests pass individually under the agents-core Vitest config.

target.title: fix(gateway): hot-reload acp config instead of restarting gateway
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102205 — adding `acp` config to `openclaw.json` triggers an infinite
gateway restart loop: gateway auto-enables acpx, detects the acp key as a
config change requiring restart, restarts, and repeats.

## Root Cause

`src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts` has no reload rule for the `acp` top-level
config key. When `acp` is added or changed, `matchRule("acp")` returns null,
defaulting to `kind: "restart"`. This triggers a full gateway restart even
though acpx runtime can be hot-reloaded via `reload-plugins`.

## Fix

Add `{ prefix: "acp", kind: "hot", actions: ["reload-plugins"] }` to
`BASE_RELOAD_RULES_TAIL`. ACP config changes now hot-reload plugins instead of
restarting the gateway.

1 line in `src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts`.

## Evidence

### End-to-End Proof — production gateway

**Before (main `4bf70be01a`):**

ACP config change triggers restart loop:

```
config change detected; evaluating reload (…acp)
config change requires gateway restart (acp)
http server listening (14 plugins: acpx, …)    ← first start ok
[restart]
http server listening (13 plugins: …)          ← acpx gone after self-restart
config change detected; evaluating reload (…acp)  ← detects again
config change requires gateway restart (acp)   ← loops forever
```

**After (this PR):**

Same ACP config. Gateway stable with acpx loaded, no self-triggered restart:

```
embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily
http server listening (14 plugins: acpx, …)    ← acpx loaded, stable
```

Gateway has been stable for 30+ minutes. No "config change requires gateway
restart" since deploying the fix.

### Regression Test

Added 2 tests in `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts`:
- `"hot-reloads plugins for acp config changes instead of restarting"` —
  verifies `acp.enabled` changes are hot-reloaded with `reloadPlugins: true`
- `"hot-reloads plugins for acp.backend config changes"` — same for
  `acp.backend`

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)  Tests  356 passed (356)
```

- [x] oxfmt + oxlint pass
- [x] git diff --check pass
- [x] Production gateway stable with acpx loaded (14 plugins)
