target.title: [codex] fix gateway restart-required reload drift
target.body:
## Summary

Read-only runtime-config drift diagnostics for gateway health. `openclaw health` (JSON and text) now reports when the running gateway's live config has drifted from the disk file on restart-required paths (model/provider/auth), so an operator can see that a disk-side repair or rotation is waiting on a restart instead of trusting a green health snapshot.

- Adds a `runtimeConfig` block to the health summary: `state: "ok" | "drift" | "unknown"`, live/disk `agents.defaults.model` labels, and the list of drifted paths (tracked: `agents.defaults.model`, `agents.defaults.models`, `agents.list`, `models`, `gateway.auth`, `auth.profiles`, `auth.order`, `secrets.providers`).
- Distinguishes unreadable/missing/invalid disk config (`state: "unknown"` with a generic message for non-admin callers) from real drift, and renders both drift and unknown states in text output.
- Gates config fingerprints (`liveSourceFingerprint`, `diskSourceFingerprint`) and the detailed disk-read error (which can contain the local config path or a parse-error excerpt) to admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) callers.
- Recomputes the drift summary on gateway health cache hits inside `mergeCachedHealthRuntimeState`, mirroring the existing delivery-queue / hot-reload-status recompute pattern, so read-scoped callers always see fresh drift state.

This PR is observability only. The hot-mode restart-required reload behavior change (honoring the restart plan instead of warn-and-keep) is intentionally NOT in this diff; it lives in the companion PR #89517 so behavior and diagnostics can be reviewed and landed independently. An earlier revision of this PR carried both concerns; they were split on 2026-06-08.

## What Problem This Solves

When `gateway.reload.mode` is `hot`, restart-required config changes (model/provider/auth) are warn-and-keep: the gateway logs `config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (...)` and keeps running on the old pinned runtime config. Nothing user-visible reported that state afterwards: `openclaw health` said everything was ok while the gateway served stale model routing or an old `gateway.auth` token that no longer matched disk. Operators debugging "my config change did nothing" had only a single gateway log line to find.

This revision also resolves the outstanding ClawSweeper P1 on this PR: `openclaw health` connects least-privilege at `operator.read` and is served from the non-sensitive 60s health cache, so a cached "ok" could mask drift that appeared right after the cache was filled. The previous head gated a cache bypass on `operator.admin`, which never fired for the read-scoped CLI. Instead of extending the bypass, the drift summary is now recomputed on every cache hit (scope-aware; fingerprints stay admin-only) and the admin bypass was deleted -- no cache bypass remains.

## Evidence

All commands below were run at head `4229b9999d` (this branch rebased onto `upstream/main` at `22376d80e1`) in a worktree on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), Node 24.

Unit/regression tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/health.snapshot.test.ts src/commands/health.test.ts
  -> Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 49 passed (49)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts
  -> Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 525 passed (525)
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                      -> clean
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json   -> clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <7 changed files>                        -> clean
oxfmt --check <7 changed files>                                      -> clean
```

New tests in this revision (`src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts`):

- `recomputes runtime-config drift on cache hits so read-scoped callers see fresh drift` -- cached "ok" + drift recompute -> `operator.read` cache hit (`{ cached: true }` respond flag asserted) returns `state: "drift"` with no fingerprints.
- `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute so fingerprints stay admin-only` -- same cache-hit path with `operator.admin` receives fingerprints; background refresh still runs.
- `drops a stale cached runtime-config summary when the recompute returns none`.

Live behavior proof (redacted, exact head): see the `Real behavior proof` section below -- a sandbox gateway built from this head shows the ok -> drift transition on the plain, non-verbose, read-scoped `openclaw health` path after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `mode: "hot"`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: plain `openclaw health` (least-privilege `operator.read`, both JSON and text) reports `runtimeConfig.state: "drift"` with `driftPaths: ["gateway.auth"]` after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"`, including when the response is served from the 60s health cache; fingerprints are omitted for read-scoped callers.

Real environment tested: sandbox gateway on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), dist built from this branch at head `4229b9999d` content, launched with `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 28934`, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config: `gateway.mode: "local"`, `gateway.auth: { mode: "token", token: "sandbox-token-OLD" }`, `gateway.reload: { mode: "hot", debounceMs: 100 }`, `agents.defaults.model: "openai/gpt-5.5"`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node dist/index.js health --json                 # call 1, fills the health cache
sed -i.bak 's/sandbox-token-OLD/sandbox-token-NEW/' $SANDBOX/openclaw.json
sleep 4
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=sandbox-token-OLD node dist/index.js health --json   # call 2, ~40s after call 1
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=sandbox-token-OLD node dist/index.js health          # text mode
```

Evidence after fix:

- Call 1 (before rotation): `"runtimeConfig": {"state": "ok", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "diskDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5"}` -- no fingerprint fields on the read-scoped path.
- Gateway reload log after `sed`:
  ```
  [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.auth.token)
  [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (gateway.auth.token)
  ```
- Call 2 (after rotation, inside the 60s `HEALTH_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` window of call 1, i.e. the cache-hit merge path): `"runtimeConfig": {"state": "drift", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "diskDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "driftPaths": ["gateway.auth"], "message": "Live gateway runtime config differs from disk for model/provider/auth paths; restart is required or pending."}` -- no fingerprint fields.
- Text mode: `Runtime config: warning (live gateway differs from disk for gateway.auth; restart required or pending; live=openai/gpt-5.5 disk=openai/gpt-5.5)`.

Observed result after fix: the ok -> drift transition is visible on the normal read-scoped `openclaw health` path immediately after the disk change, with hot mode still warn-and-keep (live gateway kept accepting `sandbox-token-OLD`); the earlier caveat about the in-process snapshot-refresh handler masking external edits no longer reproduces on current main.

What was not tested: admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) live output with fingerprints (covered by unit tests `surfaces model/provider runtime config drift ... in sensitive snapshots` and `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute`); live drift on the non-auth tracked paths such as `agents.defaults.model` or `auth.profiles` (covered by unit tests); the `{ cached: true }` respond flag is not printed by the CLI, so cache-hit routing of call 2 is established by the 60s window timing plus the deterministic handler tests.

## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

target.title: Fix/hooks agent accountid normalization
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: `POST /hooks/agent` silently drops `accountId` from incoming payloads because `HookAgentPayload` lacks the field, `normalizeAgentPayload()` never extracts it, and `dispatchAgentHook()` hand-builds a `CronJob` bypassing `normalizeCronJobCreate()`.
- Why it matters: Multi-account WhatsApp (and any channel requiring `accountId`) delivery fails silently — the caller gets a success response but the message is never sent.
- What changed: Hook dispatch now routes through `normalizeCronJobCreate()`, which promotes legacy flat fields into proper `CronDelivery` with `accountId`. `resolveCronToolPolicy()` derives `disableMessageTool` for shared-contract callers from whether the target is fully resolved (explicit mode + accountId) instead of unconditionally disabling.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): The cron-owned path (`deliveryContract: "cron-owned"`) is untouched. No changes to `normalizeCronJobCreate()` logic itself — only a JSDoc addition. No new config options or API surface.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #43866
- Related #27015, #24186, #42244, #23853, #16925, #30052, #29090

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `POST /hooks/agent` now correctly preserves `accountId` through to delivery, enabling multi-account WhatsApp delivery via hooks.
- For shared-contract hook runs with a fully resolved delivery target (explicit mode + accountId), the agent's message tool is no longer unconditionally disabled — it remains available as a fallback. The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) prevents duplicate sends.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` — the message tool was already available for shared-contract callers without delivery; this change refines *when* it stays enabled based on target resolution quality.
- Data access scope changed? `No`

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: All (server-side code path)
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / Bun
- Model/provider: Any (not model/provider-specific)
- Integration/channel (if any): WhatsApp (any multi-account channel)
- Relevant config (redacted): Hooks enabled with token, WhatsApp channel configured with multiple `accountId` connections

### Steps

1. Configure two WhatsApp connections with distinct `accountId` values.
2. Send `POST /hooks/agent` with `{ "message": "Hello", "channel": "whatsapp", "to": "1234567890", "accountId": "botnumber" }`.
3. Observe delivery result.

### Expected

- `accountId` flows through to `CronDelivery.accountId`, `resolveDeliveryTarget()` identifies the correct WhatsApp connection, and the message is delivered.

### Actual (before fix)

- `accountId` is silently dropped. Delivery fails because no connection can be identified. Caller receives success response.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

New tests added in second commit:
- `src/gateway/hooks.test.ts` — `normalizeAgentPayload` extracts and trims `accountId` (present, absent, blank)
- `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts` — integration test: `accountId` propagates into `job.delivery` via cron normalization pipeline
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 tests for shared-contract tool policy: fully resolved target (explicit + accountId → enabled), missing accountId (→ disabled), implicitly resolved target (→ disabled)

Verification: `pnpm tsgo` clean, `pnpm check` clean, all 59 tests across the 4 test files pass.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: typecheck (`pnpm tsgo`), lint/format (`pnpm check`), unit + integration tests pass for all modified test files
- Edge cases checked: blank/missing `accountId`, `normalizeCronJobCreate` returning null (guard added), implicit vs explicit delivery target mode, `mode: "none"` (verified `deliveryRequested` is already `false` so no extra clause needed)
- What you did **not** verify: live end-to-end delivery through a real WhatsApp multi-account setup; only verified through unit/integration tests and code tracing

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert both commits; the hand-built CronJob path is fully self-contained in the reverted `dispatchAgentHook()`.
- Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/hooks.ts`, `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`, `src/cron/normalize.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Hook agent dispatches returning early with "normalizeCronJobCreate returned null" warning (would indicate the normalizer rejects a payload shape it previously accepted via hand-built path).

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: `normalizeCronJobCreate()` could reject a hook payload shape that the hand-built path previously accepted, causing hook dispatches to silently no-op.
  - Mitigation: A null-return guard logs a warning and still returns a `runId` to the caller. The normalizer is well-tested and accepts all fields the hook path provides. Integration test verifies the full pipeline.

- Risk: Enabling the message tool for shared-contract callers with fully resolved targets could cause duplicate sends (agent sends via tool + automatic delivery sends again).
  - Mitigation: The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) already detects when the agent's message tool sent to the same target and skips automatic delivery. This guard predates this change and is tested.

target.title: fix: stop model catalog warning loop during sidecar refresh
target.body:
Closes #99390

AI-assisted: yes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the model-catalog warning loop where generated plugin catalog sidecar writes can fail while the private fs-safe store is protecting `catalog.json`. The reported failure is `FsSafeError: directory changed during operation`; when it lands at the generated catalog write boundary, the sidecar file can remain unwritten and dynamic provider rows stay stale or unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix now covers the owner-side write boundary directly:

- `writeModelsFileAtomicForModelsJson` reopens and retries the private store once when fs-safe reports a transient directory identity swap (`path-mismatch`) or when the same replacement race surfaces as `ENOENT` / `ENOTDIR` during the write.
- Generated plugin sidecar writes and read-only persisted catalog scans for the same agent directory share the existing process-wide model catalog file I/O queue, so readers no longer observe the sidecar tree mid-refresh.

The retry remains narrow: non-transient fs-safe failures such as denied paths still fail without retry. No provider catalog schema, runtime config, plugin SDK surface, dependency, or migration shape changes.

## User Impact

Gateway model-catalog refreshes can recover when a generated plugin catalog directory is replaced during the atomic private-store write. Dynamic provider discovery should be able to publish the refreshed sidecar instead of repeatedly logging the catalog load warning while leaving provider rows stale.

## Evidence

Exact head: `99d145c75fedffff1de4373800a799e6482998e7`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/models-config.file-mode.test.ts` (1 file, 3 tests)

target.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution can fall back to environment variables in some configurations; operators lacked a dedicated audit finding when that fallback was active.

**Concrete example:** An operator adds a world-writable `/tmp/demo-plugin` to `plugins.load.paths` and configures gateway auth via SecretRef that silently resolves from `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`. Before this PR, `openclaw security audit` did not surface either risk explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `collectPluginLoadPathAuditFindings` and wires SecretRef env-fallback diagnostics into `openclaw security audit` / doctor health contributions so misconfiguration surfaces as explicit findings instead of silent trust expansion.

Two correctness issues from ClawSweeper review were also fixed in this revision:
- **Restored `doctor:default-account-routing` contribution** — the initial squash accidentally dropped the existing opt-in doctor lint contribution for multi-account default routing; it is now preserved alongside the new `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` check added to `doctor:gateway-auth`.
- **Env propagation fix** — `isActiveGatewayTokenSurface` in `secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.ts` now accepts and forwards the caller-provided `env` to `resolveGatewayAuth`, preventing ambient `process.env` from being used for the auth-mode guard when an explicit env is injected by audit or doctor.

## User Impact

**Before:** Risky plugin load paths and active SecretRef env fallbacks could go unnoticed.

**After:** `openclaw security audit` emits `plugins.load_paths.*` and `GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRETREF_ENV_FALLBACK` findings operators can act on. No runtime behavior change unless operators remediate.

target.title: fix(auto-reply,agents/tools): strip foreign provider prefix in formatProviderModelRef
target.body:
## Bug

`formatProviderModelRef(provider, model)` only stripped a *matching* provider prefix. When `model` embedded a **different** provider prefix, the function returned a malformed result:

```
formatProviderModelRef("minimax", "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "minimax/openai/gpt-5.4"  // WRONG
formatProviderModelRef("openai",  "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "openai/gpt-5.4"          // OK (existing behavior)
```

This leaks a stale, malformed `provider/model` ref into the status banner / fallback transition rendering. End users saw the wrong provider label after a fallback attempt, even though the active runtime was correctly configured for the new provider.

## Impact

- `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.ts` is the public-facing path used by status banners.
- The same bug exists in two local copies:
  - `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.ts:159`
  - `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts:24`

## Fix

After existing same-prefix stripping, additionally check for any single `/`-delimited embedded provider segment that does **not** match the requested provider, and strip it. Same-prefix strip is now case-insensitive on the provider comparison.

```
formatProviderModelRef("minimax", "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "minimax/gpt-5.4"  // FIXED
formatProviderModelRef("OpenAI",  "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "OpenAI/gpt-5.4"  // case-insensitive
formatProviderModelRef("openai",  "gpt-5.4")        -> "openai/gpt-5.4"  // unchanged
```

Applied to all three local copies:
- `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts`

## Tests

12 new cases in `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.test.ts` + 6 new cases appended in each of:
- `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.test.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts`

Direct `vitest run` of all four test files (including the existing `fallback-state.test.ts` regression suite covering `buildFallbackNotice`, `resolveFallbackTransition`, etc.) reports **111/111 passing**.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where JSON Schema validators/defaulting would reject a valid local `$ref` into a large schema array when the referenced array index exceeded OpenClaw's config path sparse-write limit.

target.title: fix(feishu): cancel agent runs when source messages are recalled
target.body:
Related: #55691
Related: #81997

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could recall or withdraw a message but OpenClaw would still continue processing that source message and run the agent/tools. This could happen when the recall event arrived while the original message was already debounced, queued, or inside an agent dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu recall handling previously only showed up indirectly at reply delivery time, when sending a reply to a missing/recalled message could fail. This change handles the inbound `im.message.recalled_v1` event at the channel boundary, records the recalled source message in a Feishu-local runtime context, skips recalled messages before dispatch, and binds active dispatches to an abort signal so in-flight runs stop instead of producing replies.

Live testing also showed that some Feishu app configurations may not deliver `im.message.recalled_v1` to the plugin, while Feishu's message reaction API still returns code `231003` (`message not found / maybe deleted`) when the typing target is the recalled source message. The Feishu dispatcher now treats that specific channel-local signal as a conservative fallback only when the missing typing target is the inbound source message, then reuses the same recall registry, abort signal, and reply-suppression path.

The state is process-local and bounded because it only needs to coordinate nearby receive/debounce/dispatch timing within one gateway process. It does not add a core API or persistent storage surface.

## User Impact

When a Feishu user withdraws a message, OpenClaw now treats that source message as cancelled. Pending debounced messages are dropped when the recall event is delivered, active single-agent and broadcast dispatches receive an abort signal, and final replies are suppressed if the recall or missing-source fallback lands before delivery.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on chat-style surfaces could receive no visible answer when a Codex-native command approval was declined and the attempt only recorded a tool error. That empty user-addressed turn could be classified as successful terminal progress instead of a non-deliverable terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attempt terminal classifier now requires real delivery/progress evidence, such as assistant text, committed message delivery, synthesized payloads, heartbeat responses, accepted session spawns, client tool calls, yields, or async-started tool activity. A bare `lastToolError` still remains available to payload and retry logic, but it no longer proves that the user received a terminal answer.

Codex app-server trajectory finalization now applies the same non-deliverable rule for empty tool-error completions. Explicit external aborts and timeouts still record interrupted, but internally aborted empty turns without delivery evidence record `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` instead of success/interrupted without a typed terminal error.

Codex contract checked: `openai/codex@ad2012d` shows command approval responses carry `decision` values in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1329`, declined command executions are rejected/approval-denied outcomes in `codex-rs/analytics/src/reducer.rs:2262`, and malformed app-server command approval responses default to `Decline` in `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1963`.

## User Impact

Users and operators should no longer see an empty declined-native-tool turn recorded as a successful completed session solely because the attempt had a tool error. Real message delivery with a later tool error is still treated as terminal progress, so multi-target or partially delivered turns do not regress.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating videos from providers that return URL-only assets could have the CLI download provider-supplied URLs without applying the configured provider request network policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now resolves the selected provider's request policy for URL-only generated video assets and downloads them through the guarded provider HTTP path. This preserves streaming output and in-memory size caps while keeping provider request config as the opt-in path for private-network downloads.

## User Impact

CLI video generation keeps working for normal provider-hosted media, blocks private/internal download targets by default, and still permits configured private-network providers when operators opt into that request policy.

Release-note-style behavior note: URL-only generated video downloads that resolve to private/internal networks now fail closed unless the selected provider already has `models.providers.<provider>.request.allowPrivateNetwork` enabled.

target.title: [codex] fix gateway hot-mode restart reloads
target.body:
## Summary

Closes the silent-staleness hole in `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"` without changing the shipped default contract. Hot mode keeps warn-and-keep for routine restart-required config edits; two scoped behaviors layer on top:

- **`gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired: true`** (new optional key, default `false`): opt-in that delegates restart-required edits to the gateway's existing idle-aware restart path, matching `mode: "hybrid"` for the restart-required branch while keeping hot-safe edits hot.
- **Security-critical carve-out** (always on): restart reasons under `gateway.auth.*`, `auth.profiles.*` / `auth.order.*`, and top-level `secrets.*` schedule a restart even in default hot mode. Without this, a `gateway.auth.token` rotation, a doctor batch that renames `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` profiles, or a `secrets.providers.*` change on disk sits behind warn-and-keep while the runtime keeps honoring the stale credential/profile state.

The hot-mode restart policy is one shared decision (`resolveHotModeRestartDecision`) used by both the file watcher and the `config.patch` / `config.apply` RPC write path, so the two write surfaces cannot diverge. **This changes current RPC behavior in hot mode**: previously `config.patch`/`config.apply` scheduled a direct restart for any restart-required write regardless of the opt-in; now routine restart-required RPC writes return a `requiresRestart` notice without bouncing the gateway (matching the watcher's warn-and-keep contract), while security-critical and opted-in writes still schedule the direct restart.

An earlier draft of this PR made hot mode schedule restarts unconditionally; review correctly flagged that as a semantic change to the shipped `hot` contract, and the current shape supersedes it. Existing `mode: "hot"` deployments are behavior-stable on upgrade for routine edits.

## Details

- `src/gateway/config-reload-settings.ts:32`: `SECURITY_CRITICAL_RESTART_PREFIXES = ["gateway.auth", "auth.profiles", "auth.order", "secrets"]`. The `auth.profiles` / `auth.order` entries fix the review-found P1: the production repro (doctor batch renaming `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` with model routes) produced restart reasons under `auth.profiles.*` / `auth.order.*`, which are unmatched in the reload-plan rules and default to restart-required — so default hot mode dropped them with a warn. The `secrets` prefix is top-level, fixing the earlier `gateway.secrets` prefix that could never match real restart reasons; `src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts` marks `secrets.providers.*` restart-required so the carve-out has a live trigger.
- `src/gateway/config-reload-settings.ts:54`: `resolveHotModeRestartDecision` returns `"security-critical" | "opt-in" | "warn-and-keep"` and is the single owner of the hot-mode policy.
- `src/gateway/config-reload.ts:319`: the watcher's restart-required hot branch routes through the shared decision; the existing idle-aware restart machinery (`queueRestart`) remains the only watcher restart path.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts:178`: fixes the review-found P2 divergence — `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` now routes hot-mode RPC writes through the same decision instead of unconditionally direct-restarting (`scheduleDirectRestart: mode === "hot"`).
- `gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired` added to `src/config/types.gateway.ts`, `zod-schema.ts` (strict validation), `schema.help.ts`, `schema.labels.ts`.
- Regression tests pin each branch: warn-and-keep preserved on non-security edits; opt-in queues a supervised restart; security-critical auth/secrets changes restart regardless of the opt-in; the doctor-batch `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` rename auto-restarts in default hot mode (`src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts:1878`); and the RPC path is pinned three ways in `src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts:366-421` (routine write keeps running with `requiresRestart: true`, opt-in direct-restarts, auth-token write direct-restarts).
- Docs updated: `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md`, `docs/gateway/configuration.md`, `docs/gateway/index.md` describe the default, the opt-in, the carve-out, and that the policy applies to both file edits and `config.patch`/`config.apply` writes.

**Open maintainer decision:** this adds one config key on a compatibility-sensitive surface, and there is no maintainer sign-off yet on the `gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired` key. The default split (warn-and-keep stays default; auth-profile/auth/secrets changes always restart) is the proposed contract — if a different split is preferred (e.g. opt-in defaulting `true` for fresh installs only), say the word and I will adjust. The RPC alignment above is also a deliberate behavior change to today's hot-mode `config.patch` direct-restart; if maintainers prefer the RPC surface to keep direct-restarting unconditionally, that is a one-line revert in `resolveConfigRestartRequirement`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: in hot reload mode, a config write touching any restart-required key was dropped with a single `log.warn` while the gateway kept serving from the stale in-memory snapshot. Observed in production as a 4-hour silent outage where the agent kept resolving the legacy `openai-codex/gpt-5.5` model id after `openclaw doctor --fix` had migrated the on-disk config (including `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` renames) to `openai/gpt-5.5`; group messages silently dropped, admin DMs returned a canned `[agent failed]` reply. With this patch, security-critical edits (gateway auth, auth profiles/order, secrets) self-heal via restart by default, and operators can opt all restart-required edits into the same path.

- **Real environment tested**: isolated sandbox gateway on macOS (loopback port 28789), dist built from this branch at commit `d023afb9c4` (the commit introducing the opt-in + carve-out design); plus the original production incident capture on a launchd-supervised deployed gateway (`gateway-host`) documenting the pre-fix failure mode. The subsequent changes (top-level `secrets` prefix, `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` prefixes, shared RPC policy, rebase onto current main) are pinned by focused regression tests run locally at head `074e8acf36`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: sandbox scenarios (at `d023afb9c4`): start a fresh sandbox gateway from the branch dist, wait for the config watcher to settle, write one config edit, observe the reload log and process state.
  ```
  Scenario A: mode "hot" (defaults), edit gateway.bind "loopback" -> "lan"
  Scenario B: mode "hot" + autoRestartOnRequired true, same edit
  Scenario C: mode "hot" (defaults), rotate gateway.auth.token
  ```
  At final head `074e8acf36`:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**: redacted runtime log captured live from the sandbox gateway reload/restart console output (at `d023afb9c4`):
  ```
  A: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (gateway.bind)
     process state: RUNNING (pid=8610, uptime 00:14)        # warn-and-keep preserved
  B: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode scheduling restart per gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired=true (gateway.bind)
     [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
     [shutdown] started: gateway restarting
     process state: RUNNING (pid=6706, uptime 00:15)        # restarted clean
  C: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode scheduling restart for security-critical change (gateway.auth.token)
     [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
     process state: RUNNING (pid=9261, uptime 00:14)        # credential rotation propagated
  ```
  At final head `074e8acf36` (local, macOS, Node 24):
  ```
  Test Files  8 passed (8)
       Tests  474 passed (474)
  ```
  including the doctor-batch `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` watcher regression and the three hot-mode `config.patch` policy tests. `tsgo` core + core-test lanes and `oxfmt`/`oxlint` on touched files also pass.

- **Observed result after fix**: scenario A proves existing hot-mode deployments keep the shipped warn-and-keep contract with no restart. Scenario B proves the opt-in routes routine restart-required edits through the existing SIGUSR1 + clean-shutdown restart path. Scenario C proves auth rotations propagate by default, closing the credential-rotation-bypass gap. The production failure mode (`hot mode ignoring` on `auth.profiles.*` for 4 hours) is now closed at the exact prefix that caused it, pinned by the regression test at `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts:1878`.

- **What was not tested**: live sandbox-gateway captures were not re-run at the final head — the `secrets.providers.*` rotation and the doctor-batch `auth.profiles` rename scenarios are proven at head `074e8acf36` by focused regression tests only, not by a fresh end-to-end gateway capture; this is a known proof gap called out for review. Also untested: launchd auto-respawn end-to-end on hosts using `KeepAlive: { SuccessfulExit: false }` (see operator note below — the clean-exit hand-off needs a kickstart watcher on such hosts; not a regression, the pre-fix path also required manual intervention). The sandbox ran unmanaged (in-process restart mode); the managed-install launchd restart path is covered by existing integration tests.

## Operator note: launchd `SuccessfulExit=false` hosts

Hosts that set `KeepAlive: { Crashed=true, SuccessfulExit=false }` (to dodge an unrelated respawn cascade) will not auto-respawn after the restart hand-off's clean exit. The deployment fork pairs this with a 30s interval watchdog (`launchctl print` state AND port-binding check, then `launchctl kickstart -k`) — documented here so the gap flagged in review is paired with its operational answer. Hosts on default launchd `KeepAlive` semantics respawn normally and need nothing.

target.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock
target.body:
## Summary

A long-running gateway can permanently deadlock its entire agent lane on a stuck OAuth auth-refresh. The runtime auth single-flight in `auth-controller.ts` stores the in-flight refresh promise in `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight`; every model turn that needs auth does `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` **with no timeout**. If the underlying provider auth hook (`prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` -> OAuth refresh, keychain read, or cross-agent file-lock wait) never settles, `refreshInFlight` is never cleared and **every subsequent turn hangs forever** awaiting it. The process stays alive and the port stays open, so it looks healthy while no replies are produced.

Observed in production: a gateway froze mid-day right after a token hit expiry. Process alive (11d uptime, port listening) but fully idle since the freeze, zero sockets to the provider, all threads parked, one never-resolving `await`. On-disk token was valid the whole time (a fresh process pre-warmed auth in ~0.7s), and no on-disk lock was held — i.e. a pure in-memory single-flight deadlock.

This adds a hard deadline so the single-flight promise **always** settles:

- New `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline()` + `RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS` (300s) in `runtime-auth-refresh.ts`. 300s sits above the OAuth manager's own 120s call timeout plus a peer's 180s stale-lock window, so a legitimately slow cross-agent refresh still completes while a true hang is forced to reject.
- `refreshRuntimeAuth` wraps the refresh operation in that deadline; on timeout it rejects, the `.finally` clears `refreshInFlight`, and all waiters unblock with a descriptive error instead of hanging.
- The `.finally` clear is no longer gated on `generation`: a profile rotation during a slow/hung refresh must still release the handle it owns, otherwise a stale handle wedges the new generation. The existing `refreshInFlight === refreshPromise` identity guard still prevents clobbering a newer refresh.

No behavior change on the happy path (fast refresh resolves long before the deadline). The deadline is a backstop only.

## Repro / Test plan

- [x] `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline` unit tests: rejects after the deadline when work never settles (fake timers), resolves/propagates when work wins the race, passes through unbounded for non-positive timeout, and the default exceeds the OAuth call + stale-lock budget.
- [x] `auth-controller` regression test: a `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` that hangs forever sets `refreshInFlight`, then after advancing past the hard deadline the wedged handle rejects with `exceeded hard deadline` and is no longer the active in-flight handle.
- [x] Proof the test catches the bug: with the deadline neutralized (timeout `0` = unbounded), the regression test **times out / FAILS**; restored, it passes.
- [x] Current-head scoped run: see Evidence below.

Thanks @amittell.

---

## Update: complete the deadlock class (not just the refresh path)

A follow-up audit found the original commit only backstopped ONE of several entry paths into the same auth lock/gate machinery. Both remaining paths could still permanently wedge the agent lane the same way:

1. **Cold-start / profile-rotation path (critical).** `applyApiKeyInfo` (the path `initializeAuthProfile` and `advanceAuthProfile` use, and the first turn a watchdog restart lands on) awaited `resolveApiKeyForCandidate` and `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` — the exact hook that hung in production — with no deadline. A single shared local `withAuthDeadline` helper now wraps every auth boundary in `auth-controller.ts` (refresh AND cold-start), so a hung provider hook fails the turn over instead of deadlocking the lane.
2. **In-lock keychain / buildApiKey (high).** In `oauth-manager.ts`, `withRefreshCallTimeout` wrapped only the network refresh call; the in-lock keychain store load and `buildApiKey` ran un-deadlined while the cross-agent file lock was held, so a wedged keychain pinned the lock and chain-stalled every same-key refresher behind the un-timed `KeyedAsyncQueue` refresh gate (`refreshQueue.enqueue` chains each caller on the previous tail with no timeout). The whole held-lock critical section is now bounded by `OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (150s), kept strictly between the 120s call timeout and the 180s stale window.

### Added proof
- `auth-controller` cold-start regression test: a `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` that hangs forever on `initializeAuthProfile` now fails over within the deadline; **neutralizing the backstop makes the test time out / FAIL** (deadlock reproduced), confirming it catches the bug.
- `oauth-manager` invariant test pins `OAUTH_REFRESH_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS < OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS < stale`.
- All touched suites green at the current head; see Evidence below.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Current `main` still awaits `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` in `auth-controller.ts` with no timeout, and the `.finally` clear is generation-gated, so one provider auth hook, keychain read, or cross-agent lock wait that never settles leaves the in-flight handle pending forever and every later model turn deadlocks awaiting it. The gateway process stays alive and its port stays open, so monitoring sees a healthy process while the agent lane produces no replies until a manual restart. This PR makes every runtime auth boundary settle: a hard 300s deadline on the single-flight refresh and cold-start paths, an ungated in-flight-handle clear, and a 150s bound on the whole held-lock OAuth critical section so a wedged keychain or hook cannot pin the cross-agent lock and chain-stall every same-key refresher queued behind it.

## Evidence

The only conflict was `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.ts`; it was resolved by keeping main's current `doRefreshOAuthTokenWithLock` body (the `KeyedAsyncQueue` refresh queue from #99691, the refresh-contention error classification from #101573, and `readBootstrapCredential({ store, ... })`) and re-applying only the `OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` whole-section wrap on top.

Production soak on a fork: gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run this patch backported on a fork since 2026-06, and the auth-refresh deadlock that previously froze the agent lane has not recurred.

Behavior addressed: gateway agent lane permanently deadlocks when one runtime auth refresh never settles; every later model turn hangs on an un-timed `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` while the process looks healthy.

target.title: fix: stop model catalog warning loop during sidecar refresh
target.body:
Closes #99390

AI-assisted: yes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the model-catalog warning loop where generated plugin catalog sidecar writes can fail while the private fs-safe store is protecting `catalog.json`. The reported failure is `FsSafeError: directory changed during operation`; when it lands at the generated catalog write boundary, the sidecar file can remain unwritten and dynamic provider rows stay stale or unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix now covers the owner-side write boundary directly:

- `writeModelsFileAtomicForModelsJson` reopens and retries the private store once when fs-safe reports a transient directory identity swap (`path-mismatch`) or when the same replacement race surfaces as `ENOENT` / `ENOTDIR` during the write.
- Generated plugin sidecar writes and read-only persisted catalog scans for the same agent directory share the existing process-wide model catalog file I/O queue, so readers no longer observe the sidecar tree mid-refresh.

The retry remains narrow: non-transient fs-safe failures such as denied paths still fail without retry. No provider catalog schema, runtime config, plugin SDK surface, dependency, or migration shape changes.

## User Impact

Gateway model-catalog refreshes can recover when a generated plugin catalog directory is replaced during the atomic private-store write. Dynamic provider discovery should be able to publish the refreshed sidecar instead of repeatedly logging the catalog load warning while leaving provider rows stale.

## Evidence

Exact head: `99d145c75fedffff1de4373800a799e6482998e7`.

target.title: fix(outbound): restore current-conversation binding map when persist fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where plugin channels that use the generic current-conversation binding (any channel without a custom binding adapter) could route inbound messages to the wrong or a deleted session target after a failed durable write. The binding mutators — bind, touch, unbind, and expiry prune-on-read — update the process-wide in-memory binding map first and then persist it to SQLite. If the persist throws (disk full, read-only DB, transaction failure), the map is left ahead of disk. Because the map is only loaded from disk once per process (`bindingsLoaded` is a one-time flag), the diverged bindings are then served for the rest of the process lifetime — until a restart — even though the caller already received the error. Inbound messages get delivered to a stale binding (a resolved session that was actually unbound, or a target that never persisted). The one-time load path has the same weakness in the other direction: it flips `bindingsLoaded` and clears the map before the DB read completes, so a failing initial read latches an empty cache until restart. ## Why This Change Was Made Each mutating path now snapshots the in-memory map, and if the durable write throws it restores that snapshot before rethrowing, so runtime state never drifts ahead of disk. This mirrors the rollback pattern already merged for the cron scheduler in #99960 (`persistOrRestore` in `src/cron/service/ops.ts`). The unbind-by-session path snapshots after its expiry scan settles (that scan can itself persist prune deletes), so a later batch failure cannot resurrect a binding the scan already dropped from disk. The one-time load now reads into a local first and marks the cache loaded only after the read succeeds. Scope is deliberately narrow: no change to the write mechanism, the store schema, or the broader session-binding surface. The snapshot is a shallow map copy, which is sufficient because records are always replaced wholesale (never mutated in place), keeping the hot binding paths cheap. ## User Impact Operators no longer end up with a process serving conversation bindings that disagree with what is on disk after a transient storage failure. A failed mutation now leaves the in-memory state exactly as it was before the attempt, and the error still surfaces to the caller. No config, API, or behavior change on the success path. Affected paths: bind, touch, unbind by binding id, unbind by target session key, and the expiry prune-on-read. ## Evidence ### Real-behavior proof — genuine shared-SQLite write failure Drives the real production path (`bindGenericCurrentConversation` → `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`) against a real `state/openclaw.sqlite`, and injects a **genuine durable-write failure** (not a mock): `PRAGMA query_only = ON` on the production cached state connection, so the next write transaction raises `SQLITE_READONLY`. It then compares disk ground-truth (read straight from the `current_conversation_bindings` table) against what a caller is served by `resolveGenericCurrentConversationBinding`. Same recipe merged for #99960. `bind` conversation → `session-A` (persists), inject the fault, then re-`bind` the same conversation → `session-B` (write throws): **BEFORE (main `5e22787ba1`, no rollback):** ``` [fault] bind B threw : Error: attempt to write a readonly database [after] disk ground-truth : [ 'agent:codex:acp:session-A' ] [after] resolve() serves : agent:codex:acp:session-B RESULT: DIVERGENCE — caller served agent:codex:acp:session-B but disk holds agent:codex:acp:session-A (BUG present) ``` The caller saw the write error, disk still holds `session-A`, yet the in-memory map serves `session-B` — a target that never persisted. Because `bindingsLoaded` is a one-time flag, this phantom binding is served until process restart. **AFTER (this PR `bcd4668cb2`, with rollback):** ``` [fault] bind B threw : Error: attempt to write a readonly database [after] disk ground-truth : [ 'agent:codex:acp:session-A' ] [after] resolve() serves : agent:codex:acp:session-A RESULT: CONSISTENT — caller served agent:codex:acp:session-A, matches disk (rollback worked) ``` Same genuine `SQLITE_READONLY`, same surfaced error, but the map is rolled back to the last-persisted state — the caller is served what is actually on disk.
Harness (node --import tsx proof.mts, temp OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR) ```ts const CONV = { channel: "workspace", accountId: "default", conversationId: "C-real-proof" }; const SESSION_A = "agent:codex:acp:session-A"; const SESSION_B = "agent:codex:acp:session-B"; function setQueryOnly(on: boolean): void { // Toggle the production cached connection read-only so the next real write // transaction raises a genuine SQLITE_READONLY (like a read-only mount). openOpenClawStateDatabase().db.exec(`PRAGMA query_only = ${on ? "ON" : "OFF"};`); } // 1. Durably persist conversation -> SESSION_A via the real production path. await bindGenericCurrentConversation({ targetSessionKey: SESSION_A, targetKind: "session", conversation: CONV }); // 2. Inject a genuine durable-write failure on the shared SQLite connection. setQueryOnly(true); // 3. Re-bind same conversation -> SESSION_B; the real write transaction throws. try { await bindGenericCurrentConversation({ targetSessionKey: SESSION_B, targetKind: "session", conversation: CONV }); } catch (err) { /* caller sees the write error */ } // 4. Lift the fault, read disk ground-truth, observe what resolve() serves. setQueryOnly(false); const disk = /* SELECT target_session_key FROM current_conversation_bindings */; const inMemory = resolveGenericCurrentConversationBinding(CONV)?.targetSessionKey; // BEFORE: inMemory === SESSION_B (diverges from disk SESSION_A). AFTER: inMemory === SESSION_A. ```
### Focused fault-injection tests `src/infra/outbound/current-conversation-bindings.test.ts` covers each mutating path (bind, touch, unbind-by-id, unbind-by-session, prune-on-read), the mixed unbind-by-session case where an expired binding is pruned mid-scan before the batch fails, and a failing initial load that must not latch an empty cache. Same proof shape merged for the cron rollback in #99960. ``` $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/current-conversation-bindings.test.ts Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 17 passed (17) # 10 existing + 7 new ``` - `pnpm tsgo:core` — clean (0 type errors) - oxlint / oxfmt — clean

Fixes an issue where JSON Schema validators/defaulting would reject a valid local `$ref` into a large schema array when the referenced array index exceeded OpenClaw's config path sparse-write limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

JSON Pointer array indexes and OpenClaw config path array indexes have different ownership and limits. This keeps JSON Pointer parsing local to the schema helper, preserving canonical non-negative array-token parsing without applying the config writer's `100000` sparse-write cap.

target.title: fix(security): exclude test files from plugin code-safety scans (#82469)
target.body:
## Summary

`getCodeSafetySummary` in `src/security/audit-extra.async.ts` scans bundled plugin source via `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` but never passes `excludeTestFiles: true`. The option is already supported end-to-end by `skill-scanner.ts` (`TEST_FILE_NAME_PATTERN`, `TEST_DIRECTORY_NAMES`, plumbed through `walkDirWithLimit`) — it's only the caller in `audit-extra.async.ts` that leaves it off.

As a result, the deep audit (`openclaw security audit --deep`) scans plugin `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` files and produces **critical** `env-harvesting` false positives. Test files legitimately reference `process.env` for fixtures, and `fetch(` / `.post(` strings can appear inside `it("…")` descriptions or mocks; the rule fires on any file containing both, even though test files never load as the plugin runtime entry.

The reporter (operating Evolve, which relays `openclaw security audit --deep --json` findings as alerts) sees stock OC-bundled channel plugins flagged as `CRITICAL: contains dangerous code patterns`, which erodes trust in real findings.

## Fix

Two-line change in `getCodeSafetySummary`: pass `excludeTestFiles: true` to both `scanDirectoryWithSummary` call sites (cache-miss and no-cache paths). Plugin code-safety scans the runtime entry tree by design; test sources don't load at runtime and should not be scored as production credential paths.

This matches the scope the reporter recommended ("option #1") and the existing scanner contract.

Out of scope (the reporter's options #2 and #3 — making `requiresContextWindowLines` a hard gate, masking string literals in addition to comments) are rule-engine changes that touch shipped detection semantics; deferred for a separate maintainer-blessed change.

## Tests

Adds two regression tests to `src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts`:

- **spy-based** — verifies `excludeTestFiles: true` reaches `scanDirectoryWithSummary` for every plugin code-safety call site (caller-contract regression guard).
- **behavior-based** — runs the real (unmocked) scanner against a tmp plugin with a clean `index.js` plus a `provider.proxy.test.ts` containing `process.env.OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_URL` and `fetch("http://example.test/metadata")`, and asserts no `plugins.code_safety` findings are reported. This is the end-to-end fix-the-symptom test.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Deep plugin code-safety audit flagged `*.test.ts` files inside bundled plugins with critical `env-harvesting` findings (combination of `process.env` and `fetch(` / `.post(`) even though those files never load as the plugin runtime entry. This patch routes plugin scans through the existing `excludeTestFiles: true` option so test sources are skipped, matching the scanner's documented test-exclusion semantics.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, on branch `fix/code-safety-exclude-test-files-82469` at head `70bbd01976`, against upstream `main` at `b05fcad7a7`. Tests exercise the real `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` against real on-disk fixtures created in `os.tmpdir()` (no mocked-scanner result for the behavior test), so the assertion is on the actual production scanner output, not on a mock.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.ts src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

Evidence after fix:

Real vitest run output, exercising the actual `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` against a real plugin fixture on disk (no mocked scanner result for the behavior test):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.6 /Users/jinrui/Desktop/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
   Start at  18:06:30
   Duration  283ms
```

The two new tests (`passes excludeTestFiles: true to the skill scanner for plugin code-safety scans (#82469)` and `does not flag process.env + fetch( in plugin *.test.ts files (#82469)`) pass alongside the five pre-existing tests in the same file. The behavior test creates a tmp plugin with:
- `index.js`: empty `export {};` (clean runtime entry)
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: `process.env.OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_URL;` and `fetch("http://example.test/metadata");` (the exact patterns the reporter cites as triggering false positives)

…then calls `collectPluginsCodeSafetyFindings({ stateDir: tmpDir })` and asserts `findings.filter(... title.includes("test-file-noise"))` returns `[]`. With the fix removed locally, the same test fails with a critical `env-harvesting` finding pointing at `provider.proxy.test.ts:2`, which reproduces the bug shape from the issue.

Also verified independently:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts` — `Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 19 passed (19)` (no regression in the underlying scanner).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ...` — `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0, 0 errors.

Observed result after fix: The deep audit no longer produces `plugins.code_safety` critical findings sourced from `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` / `*.mock.ts` files or files inside `__tests__/`, `__mocks__/`, `__fixtures__/`, `test/`, `tests/` directories (per `TEST_DIRECTORY_NAMES` in `skill-scanner.ts`). Production runtime files are still scanned exactly as before. The `excludeTestFiles` semantics already in place for `skill-scanner.ts` are now actually applied to the plugin code-safety code path.

What was not tested: Live run against the reporter's exact `discord` channel plugin (the bundled fixture is large; the regression test instead uses a minimal plugin reproducing the same trigger pattern from the same kind of file). target.title: feat(plugin-sdk): onModelDiagnosticEvent for trusted model.* events
target.body:
## Why

Plugins subscribing to diagnostic events via `onDiagnosticEvent` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/diagnostic-runtime`) never see the `model.*` lifecycle. The public API filter at [`src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts:879-886`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts#L879-L886):

```ts
export function onDiagnosticEvent(listener: (evt: DiagnosticEventPayload) => void): () => void {
  return onInternalDiagnosticEvent((event, metadata) => {
    if (metadata.trusted || event.type === "log.record") {
      return;
    }
    listener(event);
  });
}
```

drops **every** event whose dispatcher metadata is `trusted: true`. The runtime emits `model.call.started`, `model.call.completed`, `model.call.error`, `model.usage`, and `model.failover` via `emitTrustedDiagnosticEvent`. So the entire model lifecycle is invisible to plugins.

This breaks observability/cost-attribution plugins. A telemetry bridge plugin needs:

- `model.call.completed` (provider/model identity) to populate per-call span attributes
- `model.usage` (token counts, cost) for per-call attribution

Today both subscriptions are dead code against the trusted emit paths. target.title: fix(failover): provider refusals now trigger the model fallback chain
target.body:
Fixes #98976

## What Problem This Solves
Provider refusals (Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reasons, OpenAI `content_filter` finish_reason) were never classified as a distinct FailoverReason. They fell through to the generic `LLM request failed` error path, bypassing the model fallback chain entirely — no retry on the next configured model, no auth-profile distinction, and confusing user-facing error text.

## Evidence
256 tests pass across all fix-relevant suites, including the new `anthropic-refusal.test.ts` and updated `openai-stop-reason.test.ts`, `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts`, `errors.test.ts`, `failover-matches.test.ts`, `run/failover-policy.test.ts`, `auth-profile-failure-policy.test.ts`, `failover-policy.test.ts`, `anthropic.test.ts`, `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`, and `packages/llm-core/types.test.ts`.

This fix has also been running in production on four independent gateway instances (Newhart, Victoria, Graybeard, NOVA) since 2026-07-03 with no regressions. All four instances are verified healthy on this change.

## Root cause
Provider refusals (Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reasons, OpenAI `content_filter` finish_reason) were never classified as a distinct FailoverReason. They fell through to the generic `LLM request failed` error path, bypassing the model fallback chain entirely — no retry on the next configured model, no auth-profile distinction, and confusing user-facing error text.

## Fix summary

- **New `refusal` FailoverReason** added to the `AgentRuntimeFailoverReason` union. `errorCode: "provider_refusal"` is set at the Anthropic and OpenAI transport layers.
- **Transport normalization:** Anthropic `sensitive` stop reason is treated like `refusal`; OpenAI `content_filter` maps to `errorCode: "provider_refusal"`.
- **No auth-profile rotation.** Refusals are content-scoped, not credential-scoped — the policy layer never rotates auth profiles or puts them in cooldown for a refusal.
- **No same-model retry.** The fallback skips the current model and moves to the next candidate directly.
- **Preserved probe budget.** Refusals do not consume the transient cooldown probe slot.
- **Partial-output detection.** If the model produced visible output before refusing, the output is surfaced as an error instead of silently retrying on another model (avoiding duplicate/contradictory replies).
- **Stable user copy.** When a refusal is surfaced, the user sees: *"The model declined to generate this response. Try rephrasing your request, or switch to a different model."*
- **PR #94430 boundary.** `refusal` classification takes precedence over `rate_limit` in the shared error classifier. Overlap is minimal — #94430 targets different error text patterns. A boundary comment has been added in `errors.ts`.

## Test coverage
256 tests pass across all fix-relevant suites:
| Area | Tests | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| `anthropic-refusal.test.ts` (new) | 5 | ✅ |
| `openai-stop-reason.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ |
| `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts` | 23 | ✅ |
| `errors.test.ts` | 13 | ✅ |
| `failover-matches.test.ts` | 36 | ✅ |
| `run/failover-policy.test.ts` | 39 | ✅ |
| `auth-profile-failure-policy.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ |
| `failover-policy.test.ts` | 1 | ✅ |
| `anthropic.test.ts` (incl. sensitive regression) | 39 | ✅ |
| `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` (incl. sensitive regression) | 83 | ✅ |
| `packages/llm-core/types.test.ts` | 1 | ✅ |

## Production validation
This fix has been running in production on four independent gateway instances (Newhart, Victoria, Graybeard, NOVA) since 2026-07-03 with no regressions. All four instances are verified healthy on this change.

## Maintainer notes
This PR carries a `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` label on the issue — the fix has been through staging testing (356 tests, green) and production validation across multiple gateways. We are filing this upstream as a fully tested, validated fix for the maintainer-review path (`needs-maintainer-review` / `needs-security-review`). All changes are scoped to failover policy, transport normalization, and user-facing copy — no architectural impact outside the fallback classifier and failover policy layers.

We defer entirely to maintainer judgment on whether the approach and implementation are appropriate for upstream. Happy to adjust scope, naming, or any other aspect per review feedback.

## Real behavior proof

### Expected behavior
When a provider returns a content-policy refusal (e.g. Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reason, OpenAI `content_filter` finish reason), the runner should treat this as a non-auth, non-retryable failure that walks the model fallback chain. The refusal classification must preserve any partial assistant output already delivered to the user, must not retry the same model, and must not poison shared auth-profile health.

### Actual behavior (before fix)
Provider content-policy refusals were classified as generic `unclassified` errors. This caused:
- The fallback chain to stop instead of trying the next model.
- Partial outputs from a refused turn to be discarded.
- In some configurations, the refusal could be treated as an auth failure and cool down a healthy profile.

### Repro steps
1. Configure a model that uses Anthropic (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) or OpenAI (`gpt-4.1`) and trigger a content-policy refusal.
2. Ensure a fallback model is configured in the agent/model chain.
3. Observe that before the fix the run terminates with `unclassified`; after the fix the run advances to the next model with `reason: "refusal"` and `code: "provider_refusal"`.

### Test evidence

- `vitest.agents-embedded-agent.config.ts` — 85 files, 1605 tests passed
- `vitest.cron.config.ts` — 117 files, 1232 tests passed
- `vitest.shared-core.config.ts` — 10 files, 73 tests passed

target.title: fix: mark empty tool-error turns non-deliverable
target.body:
Related: #99645

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on chat-style surfaces could receive no visible answer when a Codex-native command approval was declined and the attempt only recorded a tool error. That empty user-addressed turn could be classified as successful terminal progress instead of a non-deliverable terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attempt terminal classifier now requires real delivery/progress evidence, such as assistant text, committed message delivery, synthesized payloads, heartbeat responses, accepted session spawns, client tool calls, yields, or async-started tool activity. A bare `lastToolError` still remains available to payload and retry logic, but it no longer proves that the user received a terminal answer.

Codex app-server trajectory finalization now applies the same non-deliverable rule for empty tool-error completions. Explicit external aborts and timeouts still record interrupted, but internally aborted empty turns without delivery evidence record `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` instead of success/interrupted without a typed terminal error.

Codex contract checked: `openai/codex@ad2012d` shows command approval responses carry `decision` values in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1329`, declined command executions are rejected/approval-denied outcomes in `codex-rs/analytics/src/reducer.rs:2262`, and malformed app-server command approval responses default to `Decline` in `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1963`.

## User Impact

Users and operators should no longer see an empty declined-native-tool turn recorded as a successful completed session solely because the attempt had a tool error. Real message delivery with a later tool error is still treated as terminal progress, so multi-target or partially delivered turns do not regress.

target.title: fix(plugins): bound before_tool_call hook with a default timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The hooks listed in `DEFAULT_MODIFYING_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS_BY_HOOK`
(`src/plugins/hooks.ts`) each carry a default 15s budget —
`before_agent_run`, `before_agent_start`, `before_agent_finalize`,
`before_prompt_build`, `resolve_exec_env` — but `before_tool_call`, which gates
every tool call (block / requireApproval), is absent from the table.

Because `before_tool_call` has no budget, a plugin handler that hangs (or is very
slow) leaves the tool call awaited forever with no per-hook timeout. The only
backstop is the run-level lane idle watchdog, which fires at the configured agent
timeout — up to the 48h default (`DEFAULT_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS`) — and does not cancel
the stuck hook, so it wedges that session's turn far longer than the sibling
modifying hooks in the table and leaves the original handler promise pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

`before_tool_call` is already registered fail-closed in
`src/plugins/hook-runner-global.ts`, and `runBeforeToolCallHook` converts any
thrown hook error into a denied tool call. So a per-hook timeout is safe and
non-regressive: on timeout the hook error propagates and the tool call is
**denied**, never silently allowed. Adding `before_tool_call: 15_000` to the same
table brings it in line with its sibling modifying hooks and converts an
effectively unbounded wedge into a bounded, fail-closed denial.

## Compatibility

This changes default behavior for existing plugins: a `before_tool_call` handler
that legitimately runs longer than 15s will now have its tool call **denied**
(fail-closed) after the budget instead of the caller waiting for it to finish.
The 15s default matches the sibling modifying-hook budgets
(`before_agent_run` / `before_agent_start` / `before_agent_finalize` etc.), and a
gating hook is expected to be fast, so it should be safe for typical plugins — but
it is a maintainer-visible tradeoff, so I've flagged it rather than assumed it. If
a different budget or a per-hook override / opt-out is preferred, this can be made
configurable.

## User Impact

A hung or slow `before_tool_call` plugin handler can no longer wedge a session's
turn for hours. After 15s the tool call is denied (fail-closed) and the run
proceeds to its normal error handling, instead of blocking the lane until the
agent timeout.

## Evidence

**Real-behavior proof (real wall-clock timers, no mocks of the timeout
mechanism).** A hung `before_tool_call` handler (`() => new Promise(() => {})`)
was driven through the shipped production runner factories with real timers, and
the tool call was denied at ~15s:

```
=== BEFORE (current main: before_tool_call has no timeout budget) ===
t=0.00s   tool call issued; hung before_tool_call handler running
t=17.01s  settled=pending  (handler invoked 1x)
RESULT: still PENDING after 17.01s — no per-hook bound. On main the only
        backstop is the lane idle watchdog (up to 48h), so the turn is wedged.

=== AFTER (fix: real global runner, default 15s + fail-closed) ===
t=0.00s   tool call issued; hung before_tool_call handler running
t=15.03s  tool call DENIED (promise rejected)
          error: [hooks] before_tool_call handler from proof-hung-plugin
                 failed: timed out after 15000ms
RESULT: PASS — hung before_tool_call denied at ~15s (elapsed 15.03s,
        timeout-message=true, fail-closed deny=true)
```

- **AFTER** boots the real global hook runner via
  `initializeGlobalHookRunner` (`src/plugins/hook-runner-global.ts`) — the exact
  wiring the gateway uses — with **no per-call overrides**: both the 15s budget
  (the added `DEFAULT_MODIFYING_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS_BY_HOOK` entry) and the
  deny-on-timeout come from shipped code. The hung handler is denied after a real
  ~15s with the `timed out after 15000ms` hook error.
- **BEFORE** uses the same production `createHookRunner` with no positive budget
  for `before_tool_call` (faithful to current main, where the key is absent):
  the same hung handler is still pending after 17s — past where the fix denies —
  confirming today's unbounded wedge.

**Unit test.** New test in `src/plugins/hooks.before-tool-call.test.ts`: a hung
`before_tool_call` handler under the fail-closed policy (matching the global
runner) times out at 15s and the run **rejects** (tool denied), with the expected
`timed out after 15000ms` hook error. The existing `before_tool_call`
ordering/mutation/approval tests and the adjacent `hook-runner-global` /

(`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files>`). Changed-lane lint/typecheck/test gates
run in CI.

target.title: fix(line): cap user profile cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unbounded in-process **`userProfileCache`** in the LINE send path (`extensions/line/src/send.ts`). Profile lookups are cached for 5 minutes (TTL) but had no entry-count cap, so gateways serving many distinct LINE users accumulate Map entries indefinitely.

**Concrete scenario:** A LINE gateway processing inbound messages from 10 000 distinct users over several hours caches each `getUserProfile` result. With no size cap, the cache grows to 10 000+ entries and does not shrink until the gateway restarts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extracts a `cacheLineUserProfile` writer helper that:

1. Deletes the existing entry for `userId` when present (refreshes insertion order for re-fetched profiles)
2. Sets the new profile entry (newest insertion position)
3. Calls `pruneMapToMaxSize` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`) to evict the oldest-inserted entry until the map is at or under **1 024 entries**

The cap constant `LINE_USER_PROFILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 1024` is wired only in `cacheLineUserProfile`; TTL logic in `getUserProfile` is unchanged.

**Eviction semantics:** The cache uses insertion-order-on-write eviction, not pure LRU. Entries are moved to newest position when they are re-fetched from the LINE API (TTL miss or force-fetch). Read-only cache hits do not refresh insertion order, so a valid cached profile that has not been re-fetched can be evicted when 1 024 newer distinct users fill the cache. This is the documented behavior of `pruneMapToMaxSize` (first iterated entry → oldest insertion → evicted first) and is an acceptable trade-off for bounded memory without scan overhead on every read.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-lived LINE gateways accumulate one `userProfileCache` entry per distinct user indefinitely, growing Map memory without bound.

**After:** The cache is capped at 1 024 entries. Entries evict in insertion order once the cap is exceeded. A re-fetched profile is refreshed to newest position; a cache hit does not change its eviction rank. Behavior is unchanged for the first 1 024 distinct users seen in a gateway lifecycle.

## Evidence

- `extensions/line/src/send.ts:28` — `LINE_USER_PROFILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 1024`
- `extensions/line/src/send.ts:33–43` — `cacheLineUserProfile`: delete + set + `pruneMapToMaxSize`
- `extensions/line/src/send.ts:524` — `getUserProfile` now calls `cacheLineUserProfile` instead of bare `userProfileCache.set`
- `extensions/line/src/send.ts:540–542` — `resetLineUserProfileCacheForTests` export (test isolation only)
- `src/infra/map-size.ts:13` — `pruneMapToMaxSize` iterates insertion order and deletes the first key until the map fits
- Diff: +39/−1 across 2 files (source +17, tests +21, plus one `beforeEach` reset line)

### Behavior proof

All tests below were run against PR head commit `aaf69e5d98116c41a40206f3b0f66aaaef4271a0` on Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2 (macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, 2026-07-08T05:24:12Z). The SHA can be independently verified:

```bash

# aaf69e5d98116c41a40206f3b0f66aaaef4271a0
```

 ↓ |extension-line| ... > LINE send helpers > caches profile results by default

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.70s

2. Fetch `U-fill-1` … `U-fill-1024` → **1024** more API calls (**1025** total; cache now at cap 1024 with `U-first` evicted)

target.title: fix(qqbot): add actionable setup error guidance
target.body:
## Summary

Add shared QQBot setup guidance to the user-facing errors that currently leave users at a dead end when credentials or platform access fail.

## Issue/Motivation

Fixes #65868.

Current main still emits terse QQBot failures in the exact paths called out by the issue:
- missing gateway/outbound credentials only say `QQBot not configured (missing appId or clientSecret)`;
- token endpoint failures expose the raw Open Platform JSON without telling the user which OpenClaw settings to fix;
- API/network errors include the low-level failure but no setup path.

## Changes

- Add a small shared QQBot setup-guidance helper that points users to `QQBOT_APP_ID`, `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET`, and the QQBot setup docs.
- Use that guidance for missing gateway/outbound credentials.
- Append the guidance to token endpoint failures when `access_token` is absent.
- Append the guidance to structured QQBot API errors and network errors.
- Add regression tests for token, structured API, and network error messages.

## Testing

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/token.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/api-client.test.ts` — passed (2 files, 11 tests)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/token.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/api-client.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/setup-guidance.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/outbound.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/token.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/api-client.test.ts` — passed (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed
- staged diff secret scan — passed; no credential-looking additions

Note: full `pnpm lint:extensions` was attempted twice after installing dependencies, but timed out locally after 300s and 600s respectively, so I used the equivalent targeted oxlint command for the changed QQBot files.

## What Problem This Solves

QQBot users hitting missing credentials, invalid Open Platform token responses, or API/network failures now get actionable recovery guidance in the error itself instead of only a terse/raw failure. The message names the exact OpenClaw environment variables to configure and links to the QQBot channel docs.

## Evidence

- Source-level repro on current main before this change:
  - `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts` threw only `QQBot not configured (missing appId or clientSecret)`.
  - `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/outbound.ts` returned the same terse message for text/media sends.
  - `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/token.ts` threw `Failed to get access_token: ${JSON.stringify(data)}` when the token response omitted `access_token`.
  - `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/api-client.ts` emitted low-level API/network errors without setup guidance.
- Regression tests assert the new messages include `QQBOT_APP_ID`, `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/qqbot` for token, structured API, and network failures.
- Validation commands run locally:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/token.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/api-client.test.ts` — passed (2 files, 11 tests)
  - `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
  - targeted oxlint on all changed QQBot files — passed (0 warnings, 0 errors)
  - `git diff --cached --check` — passed
  - staged diff secret scan — passed
