target.title: fix(security): exclude test files from plugin code-safety scans (#82469)
target.body:
## Summary

`getCodeSafetySummary` in `src/security/audit-extra.async.ts` scans bundled plugin source via `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` but never passes `excludeTestFiles: true`. The option is already supported end-to-end by `skill-scanner.ts` (`TEST_FILE_NAME_PATTERN`, `TEST_DIRECTORY_NAMES`, plumbed through `walkDirWithLimit`) — it's only the caller in `audit-extra.async.ts` that leaves it off.

As a result, the deep audit (`openclaw security audit --deep`) scans plugin `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` files and produces **critical** `env-harvesting` false positives. Test files legitimately reference `process.env` for fixtures, and `fetch(` / `.post(` strings can appear inside `it("…")` descriptions or mocks; the rule fires on any file containing both, even though test files never load as the plugin runtime entry.

The reporter (operating Evolve, which relays `openclaw security audit --deep --json` findings as alerts) sees stock OC-bundled channel plugins flagged as `CRITICAL: contains dangerous code patterns`, which erodes trust in real findings.

## Fix

Two-line change in `getCodeSafetySummary`: pass `excludeTestFiles: true` to both `scanDirectoryWithSummary` call sites (cache-miss and no-cache paths). Plugin code-safety scans the runtime entry tree by design; test sources don't load at runtime and should not be scored as production credential paths.

This matches the scope the reporter recommended ("option #1") and the existing scanner contract.

Out of scope (the reporter's options #2 and #3 — making `requiresContextWindowLines` a hard gate, masking string literals in addition to comments) are rule-engine changes that touch shipped detection semantics; deferred for a separate maintainer-blessed change.

## Tests

Adds two regression tests to `src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts`:

- **spy-based** — verifies `excludeTestFiles: true` reaches `scanDirectoryWithSummary` for every plugin code-safety call site (caller-contract regression guard).
- **behavior-based** — runs the real (unmocked) scanner against a tmp plugin with a clean `index.js` plus a `provider.proxy.test.ts` containing `process.env.OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_URL` and `fetch("http://example.test/metadata")`, and asserts no `plugins.code_safety` findings are reported. This is the end-to-end fix-the-symptom test.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Deep plugin code-safety audit flagged `*.test.ts` files inside bundled plugins with critical `env-harvesting` findings (combination of `process.env` and `fetch(` / `.post(`) even though those files never load as the plugin runtime entry. This patch routes plugin scans through the existing `excludeTestFiles: true` option so test sources are skipped, matching the scanner's documented test-exclusion semantics.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, on branch `fix/code-safety-exclude-test-files-82469` at head `70bbd01976`, against upstream `main` at `b05fcad7a7`. Tests exercise the real `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` against real on-disk fixtures created in `os.tmpdir()` (no mocked-scanner result for the behavior test), so the assertion is on the actual production scanner output, not on a mock.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.ts src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

Evidence after fix:

Real vitest run output, exercising the actual `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` against a real plugin fixture on disk (no mocked scanner result for the behavior test):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.6 /Users/jinrui/Desktop/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
   Start at  18:06:30
   Duration  283ms
```

The two new tests (`passes excludeTestFiles: true to the skill scanner for plugin code-safety scans (#82469)` and `does not flag process.env + fetch( in plugin *.test.ts files (#82469)`) pass alongside the five pre-existing tests in the same file. The behavior test creates a tmp plugin with:
- `index.js`: empty `export {};` (clean runtime entry)
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: `process.env.OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_URL;` and `fetch("http://example.test/metadata");` (the exact patterns the reporter cites as triggering false positives)

…then calls `collectPluginsCodeSafetyFindings({ stateDir: tmpDir })` and asserts `findings.filter(... title.includes("test-file-noise"))` returns `[]`. With the fix removed locally, the same test fails with a critical `env-harvesting` finding pointing at `provider.proxy.test.ts:2`, which reproduces the bug shape from the issue.

Also verified independently:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts` — `Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 19 passed (19)` (no regression in the underlying scanner).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ...` — `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0, 0 errors.

Observed result after fix: The deep audit no longer produces `plugins.code_safety` critical findings sourced from `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` / `*.mock.ts` files or files inside `__tests__/`, `__mocks__/`, `__fixtures__/`, `test/`, `tests/` directories (per `TEST_DIRECTORY_NAMES` in `skill-scanner.ts`). Production runtime files are still scanned exactly as before. The `excludeTestFiles` semantics already in place for `skill-scanner.ts` are now actually applied to the plugin code-safety code path.

What was not tested: Live run against the reporter's exact `discord` channel plugin (the bundled fixture is large; the regression test instead uses a minimal plugin reproducing the same trigger pattern from the same kind of file). Effect on installed-skill code-safety scans was not changed here — the same `getCodeSafetySummary` is used by `collectInstalledSkillsCodeSafetyFindings`, so installed skills now also get test-file exclusion; this matches the conceptual contract (skill runtime entry, not its specs) but the issue is plugin-focused so installed-skill end-to-end was not separately re-verified. Options #2 (hard-gate `requiresContextWindowLines`) and #3 (mask string literals) from the issue are deferred.

target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): metrics and logs posted to the traces endpoint when the shared OTLP endpoint is signal-qualified
target.body:
Closes #98886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configuring a single shared OTLP `endpoint` that ends in a signal path (e.g. a hosted frontend URL such as `https://host/api/public/otel/v1/traces`) would have **metrics and logs POSTed to the traces endpoint** when more than one signal was enabled. OTLP backends then reject the wrong wire type (Langfuse logs `invalid wire type 7`), so metrics and logs never arrive.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveOtelUrl` now normalizes only the *shared* endpoint: when it already ends in `/v1/<signal>`, the trailing segment is rewritten to match the signal being resolved (`/v1/traces` -> `/v1/metrics` or `/v1/logs`), preserving any query string or fragment. Explicit per-signal overrides (`*Endpoint` config and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT` env) are still used verbatim, and bare base URLs keep the existing append behavior — so no currently-working configuration changes.

This is the same design as the open #98911 (and the closed #98899 / #98915). A fresh PR is opened because #98911 has been stale since Jul 2 (merge-conflicting, all CI checks cancelled, not mergeable) with no maintainer activity. Happy to close this in favor of a rebased #98911 if a maintainer prefers — the goal is just to land a correct, mergeable, green fix. This PR also adds a docs note and a regression test that fails on the unfixed code.

## User Impact

Operators can point a single shared `endpoint` at a signal-qualified OTLP URL and have traces, metrics, and logs each delivered to the correct path, without needing per-signal `*Endpoint` overrides.

**Behavior change (upgrade note):** A shared `endpoint` (or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`) that already ends in `/v1/<signal>` is now rewritten per signal (`/v1/traces` → `/v1/metrics` / `/v1/logs`) instead of being reused verbatim for every signal. This is a no-op for traces-only setups and fixes multi-signal setups where metrics/logs previously went to the traces path and were rejected; operators who need all signals on one URL can still use per-signal `*Endpoint` overrides, which stay verbatim.

## Evidence

- New regression test `normalizes a shared signal-qualified endpoint for the other signals` (shared `.../v1/traces?timeout=30s`, traces + metrics + logs): traces unchanged, metrics -> `.../v1/metrics?timeout=30s`, logs -> `.../v1/logs?timeout=30s`. Verified it **fails on the pre-fix source** (metric URL resolved to `.../v1/traces`) and passes after.
- New lock-in test `preserves an explicit per-signal signal-qualified endpoint verbatim` guards the preserve path against future over-normalization.
- `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`: **108 passed** (`vitest.extension-misc.config.ts`); `oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix: tasks.list re-sorts the whole registry on every Control UI poll
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Control UI's `tasks.list` poll stalls the gateway event loop on busy installs. Each call cloned and O(n log n) sorted every task record by `createdAt`, then immediately re-sorted the filtered set by last activity and sliced a bounded page — so the `createdAt` sort was thrown away, and the full re-sort ran across the entire registry on every poll. On gateways with thousands of accumulated completed/failed tasks this produced a noticeable event-loop stall per RPC (#101716).

Closes #101716.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes remove the wasted work while keeping the wire output byte-for-byte identical:

1. **Skip the discarded `createdAt` sort.** A new `listTaskRecordsUnsorted()` returns cloned records without the registry's newest-created sort (and the `insertionIndex` bookkeeping that only exists to support it). The `tasks.list` handler re-sorts by last activity anyway, so the registry sort was pure waste.
2. **Only sort the window the client needs.** `partialSortTopK` quickselects the `cursor + limit` window and fully sorts just that window — O(n + k log k) instead of O(n log n) — with a full-sort fallback when `k >= n`.

The page comparator (`taskUpdatedAt` desc, `taskId` asc) is unchanged, and since `taskId` is unique the order is a total order, so quickselect's non-stability cannot change results.

## User Impact

Operators of busy gateways get snappier Control UI task-list polling and no per-poll event-loop stalls as the task registry grows over days of uptime. Paging behavior and ordering are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.test.ts` → **9 passed**.
- New pagination test (pages past the first page) and a new equivalence test that pages through 12 records with mixed distinct/duplicate `lastEventAt` values and asserts the collected order across all pages exactly matches a full-sort reference — exercising both the partial-sort (`k < n`) path and the full-sort (`k >= n`) path, plus the `taskId` tie-break. Repeated 6× to confirm the randomized quickselect pivot is not flaky.
- `oxlint` clean; `tsgo:test:src` (test typecheck) clean.

## Notes

This combines and completes two earlier partial attempts (both still open with failing checks):
- #102132 added `listTaskRecordsUnsorted()` but left the full handler re-sort in place (`check-test-types` failed).
- #102118 added `partialSortTopK` but still called the sorted `listTaskRecords()` (`check-lint` failed).

This PR takes both ideas, resolves both CI failures, and adds the equivalence regression neither had. Happy to rework or fold into one of those if a maintainer prefers.

target.title: feat(session-lock): opt-in diagnostics for embedded session fence takeovers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opt-in observability for embedded-attempt **session fence takeovers**.

When a session `.jsonl` changes under a released prompt lock in a way the fence cannot explain as an owned in-process write, the controller tears the attempt down by throwing `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` — which carries only the file path. Across the **10 takeover throw sites** in `attempt.session-lock.ts` there was previously **no diagnostic at all** (the file has no logger). In production this makes a takeover effectively opaque: the only way to learn *which* check tripped and *what* file state could not be reconciled was to patch the installed bundle and add logging by hand.

The gap is real. A released-prompt takeover can fire when a legitimate in-process writer (e.g. an outbound delivery-queue transcript append) races the fence window, and without the fingerprints and owned-write history it looks identical to a genuine external editor.

## What Changed

Every takeover-detection point now goes through a small `markSessionTakeover(reason, current?)` helper. **Behaviour is unchanged** — it sets the same `takeoverDetected` flag and the same error is still thrown. When `session-lock` debug logging is enabled it additionally emits one structured record:

- `reason` — which check tripped (`unexplained-session-file-change`, `owned-write-merge-rejected`, `write-lock-acquire-error`, …)
- `sessionFile`, `fenceActive`, `fenceGeneration`
- `expectedFingerprint` vs `currentFingerprint` (dev/ino/size/mtimeNs/ctimeNs, stringified so the record survives any JSON transport)
- `ownedWriteCount` and `lastOwnedWriteGeneration`

It is gated behind `isEnabled("debug")`, so there is **zero overhead when the subsystem is not in debug**. No new env var — it uses the existing `session-lock` subsystem logger.

## Evidence

**Live diagnostic output.** Exercising a real external-append takeover (append to the session file while the prompt lock is released, then take the write lock) now emits, via the `session-lock` logger:

```
embedded session fence takeover: unexplained-session-file-change
{
  "reason": "unexplained-session-file-change",
  "sessionFile": ".../session.jsonl",
  "fenceActive": true,
  "fenceGeneration": 1,
  "expectedFingerprint": { "exists": true, "dev": "16777231", "ino": "200684408", "size": "19", "mtimeNs": "1783519408483846902", "ctimeNs": "1783519408483846902" },
  "currentFingerprint":  { "exists": true, "dev": "16777231", "ino": "200684408", "size": "63", "mtimeNs": "1783519408484811232", "ctimeNs": "1783519408484811232" },
  "ownedWriteCount": 0,
  "lastOwnedWriteGeneration": null
}
```

The record immediately tells the story: **same inode**, size grew `19 → 63` (a plain append), `ownedWriteCount: 0` — an unpublished writer advanced the file. That is exactly the signal needed to distinguish a benign in-process append (which would carry an owned-write generation) from a real external editor.

**Tests.** New `attempt.session-lock.diagnostics.test.ts`:
- emits the structured diagnostic (reason + fingerprints) on a real takeover,
- stays silent when `session-lock` debug logging is disabled (zero overhead),
- stays silent when no takeover occurs.

The full existing `attempt.session-lock.test.ts` suite (222 tests) passes unchanged, confirming the flag/throw behaviour is untouched. `oxlint` and a scoped `tsgo --noEmit` are clean on the changed files.

target.title: [Bug]: Agent heartbeat routes to wrong agent's session instead of its own
target.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary


Configured agent's heartbeat executes in default agent's session regardless of isolatedSession setting

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an agent with a heartbeat configuration:

```json
{
  "name": "historian2",
  "heartbeat": {
    "every": "10m",
    "activeHours": { "start": "00:00", "end": "24:00", "timezone": "Asia/Tokyo" },
    "includeReasoning": true,
    "target": "discord",
    "directPolicy": "allow",
    "to": "user:discord-user-id",
    "lightContext": false,
    "isolatedSession": true,
    "skipWhenBusy": false
  }
}
```

2. Put a unique logging command in ~/.openclaw/workspace-historian2/HEARTBEAT.md:

```
the agent must execute following command `mkdir -p /home/node/.openclaw/workspace-historian2/logs && date >> /home/node/.openclaw/workspace-historian2/logs/heartbeat.log`
```

3. Put a different logging command in the default workspace's HEARTBEAT.md:

```
the agent must execute following command `mkdir -p /home/node/.openclaw/workspace/logs && date >> /home/node/.openclaw/workspace/logs/heartbeat.log`
```

4. Wait for the heartbeat to fire (or trigger manually with openclaw system event --text "..." --mode now)

5. Check which workspace's HEARTBEAT.md was executed


### Expected behavior

When an agent (e.g., `historian2`) has a heartbeat configured, the heartbeat should execute **in that agent's own session** and read **that agent's own `HEARTBEAT.md`** from its workspace.

### Actual behavior

The heartbeat executes in the **default agent's session** (`main`) and reads the **default agent's `HEARTBEAT.md`** instead of the configured agent's `HEARTBEAT.md`. This is a **routing bug**, not a prompt or model accuracy issue.

### OpenClaw version

v2026.6.11

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04LTS

### Install method

docker

### Model

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (LM Studio)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw->docker bridge->home lan->Other Windows PC's LM Studio

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

### Key findings

- isolatedSession: true — historian2's session directory is empty (ephemeral), default's logs/heartbeat.log was created
- isolatedSession: false — same result: historian2's logs/heartbeat.log was NOT created, default's logs/heartbeat.log WAS created
- Both settings produce the same result: the default agent's HEARTBEAT.md is executed
- openclaw status --deep shows Last heartbeat: ok-token · discord, confirming the heartbeat ran successfully — just in the wrong agent's session

### `openclaw status --deep` output

│ Heartbeat │ disabled (main), disabled (historian), 10m (historian2) │
│ Last heartbeat │ ok-token · 1m ago · discord │

### Additional evidence

- `openclaw system heartbeat last` shows `"status": "skipped"` when `target: "last"` (no last session exists)
- Changing `target` to `"discord"` resolved the skip issue
- Historian2's session directory is empty (only `sessions.json`), confirming isolated sessions are ephemeral
- The heartbeat turn log appears in the **default agent's session directory**, not historian2's


### Impact and severity

- Multi-agent setups where each agent has its own `HEARTBEAT.md` will not work as documented
- Agents cannot have independent periodic tasks via heartbeat
- The documented behavior ("Heartbeats run in the agent's main session by default") does not match actual behavior


### Additional information

- `openclaw system heartbeat last` shows `"status": "skipped"` when `target: "last"` (no last session exists)
- Changing `target` to `"discord"` resolved the skip issue
- Historian2's session directory is empty (only `sessions.json`), confirming isolated sessions are ephemeral
- The heartbeat turn log appears in the **default agent's session directory**, not historian2's

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a gap where users could install plugins from npm, git, local paths, local archives, npm-pack tarballs, or marketplace sources without a clear install-time acknowledgement that the source is outside ClawHub review and trust metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a distinct non-ClawHub provenance acknowledgement path for plugin installs while leaving ClawHub release-risk acknowledgement, `security.installPolicy`, and lifecycle `before_install` hooks intact. ClawHub installs continue without the non-ClawHub warning; non-ClawHub CLI, deprecated hooks alias, and Crestodian-approved install flows now forward the explicit acknowledgement state.

## User Impact

Interactive users now see a warning before installing from sources that are not ClawHub-reviewed. Noninteractive users can proceed only after explicitly passing `--acknowledge-non-clawhub-install`, making automated installs intentional and auditable.

## Evidence

- Non-ClawHub install sources now emit an outside-ClawHub-review warning and require prompt/flag acknowledgement before installer side effects.
- Explicit ClawHub installs do not show the non-ClawHub warning and keep their separate ClawHub risk acknowledgement behavior.

target.title: Fix LINE webhook retryable acknowledgement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LINE webhook handlers acknowledged signed event requests before knowing whether local dispatch even started. If the handler rejected immediately, OpenClaw still returned 200, so LINE would not redeliver a retryable webhook even though the event was not accepted.

The same early-ACK shape existed in the standalone Express middleware, the Node webhook handler, and the shared multi-account monitor route.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change introduces a bounded dispatch-acceptance step for LINE webhooks. Each entrypoint starts event handling, waits one event-loop turn to surface startup-time rejection as a 500 response, then acknowledges with 200 once dispatch is accepted. If processing continues asynchronously, later failures are still logged in the background instead of holding the provider HTTP response for the full agent turn.

The LINE message adapter now defaults to `after_agent_dispatch` while preserving shipped `after_receive_record` support. The exported Node/Express handlers and shared monitor route have a real `after_receive_record` path for compatibility, and unsupported policy inputs normalize to the default dispatch-acceptance behavior instead of hanging.

## User Impact

Immediate LINE webhook dispatch failures can now trigger provider redelivery instead of being swallowed behind a 200 response. Normal successful turns still ACK quickly after local dispatch starts, avoiding long webhook waits while the agent run continues. Existing consumers that inspect or choose `after_receive_record` remain compatible.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/webhook-node.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts` (60 tests passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts` (28 tests passed)
- Local HTTP transcript through `createLineNodeWebhookHandler`:
  - slow dispatch: `status=200`, body `{"status":"ok"}`, response returned before the pending handler was released
  - immediate dispatch failure: `status=500`, body `{"error":"Internal server error"}`
- `git diff --check -- extensions/line/src/webhook-ack.ts extensions/line/src/webhook.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-node.ts extensions/line/src/outbound.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-node.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts docs/channels/line.md`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (clean after preserving `after_receive_record` support and narrowing/normalizing the exposed ACK policy)

target.title: Fix Telegram durable partial final handling
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram durable final delivery can return `status: "failed"` with `sentBeforeError: true` when the first chunk of a final reply was already visible but a later chunk failed. The Telegram dispatch path threw that error without preserving the visible-send state, so spooled replay/error handling could treat the turn as if no final answer was delivered and retry or send fallback text after the user had already seen part of the final reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable delivery contract already marks partial sends with `sentBeforeError` / `visibleReplySent`. This change makes Telegram honor that contract in its custom durable-final path by marking the final answer as delivered before surfacing the error. Pure durable failures still use the existing failure path.

Regression coverage now exercises both sides of the state boundary: partial-visible durable failures complete without duplicate fallback/retry, while pure no-send durable failures remain retryable for spooled replay.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive duplicate fallback text or replayed Telegram turns after a durable final reply was partially visible. Real no-send durable failures still fail normally and remain retryable where appropriate.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts` (173 tests passed)
- Fault-injected durable-send regression coverage:
  - partial-visible final failure (`sentBeforeError: true`) completes without fallback/retry and annotates visible-send metadata
  - pure no-send final failure remains `failed-retryable` with no fallback when spooled replay suppresses fallback
- `git diff --check -- extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)

- Migration needed? (`No`)

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.
